added.title: Forward Deployed Engineer
added.description:
Exodigo is the leading underground mapping solution for non-intrusive discovery. Our platforms combine multi-sensor fusion, 3D imaging, and AI technologies to create complete, accurate underground maps that enable confident decision-making for customers across the built world. We transform the project lifecycle for our customers, who include key community stakeholders in the utilities, transportation and government sectors.

We are experiencing sky-rocketing growth and closed a historically large $96M Series B round in July of 2025

.

Job description:

Exodigo engineers the underground without digging. Our platform combines multi-sensor fusion and AI to produce complete, accurate 3D maps of buried utilities, foundations, and geotechnical conditions, which utilities, transportation agencies, and engineering firms use to plan, design, and build with confidence. Behind every map is a team of civil engineers, BIM modelers, and mapping specialists who turn raw subsurface data into engineering-grade deliverables.

We are looking for an AI BIM Engineer to help that team move faster, stay consistent, and scale with our growth. You will work alongside our Mapping, Delivery, and Engineering Services teams, learn how a project moves from field scan through interpretation to Civil 3D and OpenRoads models and client-ready utility maps, and find where AI can take on the repetitive work so our engineers can focus on engineering judgment.

This is a hands-on, builder role. You will scope the problem, build the solution, ship it into live projects, and stay with it until it becomes part of how the team works. You will be the bridge between engineers who know the underground deeply and the AI agents that can amplify them: you can discuss utility quality levels, model QA/QC, and client CAD standards in the morning, and write a new integration for an AI agent in the afternoon. What you learn on our projects will shape the AI capabilities we give every team.

What You'll Do

Embed with engineering teams

Work side by side with highway, structures, water, and site development teams to understand their design processes, tools, standards, and pain points.
Lead discovery sessions with engineers and project leads, and translate what you hear into clearly scoped, prioritized opportunities for AI and automation.
Own delivery end to end: from first conversation and rapid prototype through to a stable tool in daily production use.
Coach engineers on using AI effectively and safely in their work, through hands-on sessions, office hours, and one-on-one support.

Turn expertise into repeatable workflows

Partner with senior engineers to capture their know-how (checking procedures, design criteria, QA/QC steps, naming and modeling standards) as reusable AI workflows, prompts, and playbooks.
Design workflows that are repeatable and reviewable: clear inputs, clear outputs, and an engineer in the loop wherever professional judgment or sign-off is required.
Build evaluation sets from real project data so we can measure whether a workflow is accurate and reliable before it scales.
Document what you build and help teams own and extend their workflows themselves.

Extend what our AI agents can do

Design and build integrations that let AI agents read, query, and act on civil engineering data: BIM models, alignments, surfaces, pipe networks, drawings, specifications, and project records.
Develop tools and connectors on top of platforms such as Autodesk Civil 3D, Revit, and Autodesk Platform Services / ACC, Bentley OpenRoads and iTwin, and open formats such as IFC and LandXML.
Build automations with Dynamo, pyRevit, Python, and C#/.NET where a deterministic script is the right answer and expose them as capabilities an AI agent can call.
Make sound trade-offs between speed, scope, and quality, and keep everything you ship secure, version-controlled, and maintainable.

Close the loop

Spot patterns across teams and turn one-off solutions into shared, reusable capabilities.
Feed field insights back to our digital, IT, and data teams to shape platform priorities and roadmap.
Contribute to our AI governance, data-handling, and BIM standards so adoption stays responsible as it grows.

Requirements:

Degree in Civil Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
4+ years combining software development with BIM, CAD, or digital delivery work, ideally on infrastructure or civil projects.
Strong coding skills in Python, plus experience with C#/.NET or TypeScript.
Hands-on experience automating BIM workflows using tools such as Dynamo, pyRevit, the Civil 3D or Revit APIs, or Autodesk Platform Services.
Practical experience building with large language models: prompt and workflow design, tool or function calling, retrieval over documents, and evaluating model output.
A working understanding of civil design deliverables: alignments and profiles, corridors, grading, drainage and utility networks, sheet production, and model coordination.
Comfort working directly with end users: you listen first, explain clearly to non-technical audiences, and build trust by shipping.
Ownership and a bias for action. You are happy working in ambiguity, scoping your own work, and seeing it through to adoption.

Nice to Have

Experience building agent integrations, for example using the Model Context Protocol (MCP) or similar tool frameworks.
Familiarity with openBIM and infrastructure data standards such as IFC 4.3, LandXML, and ISO 19650.
Experience with Bentley OpenRoads, OpenFlows, or iTwin; Navisworks; or GIS platforms such as ArcGIS.
Experience with document AI on drawings, specifications, and reports, including PDF and OCR pipelines.
Background as a practicing civil engineer or BIM coordinator before moving into software.
Experience delivering training or leading change-management programs in an engineering organization.

Learn more:

What Success Looks Like

In your first year, you will have:

Embedded with several project teams and built a clear map of where AI can save the most time and reduce the most risk.
Shipped AI workflows that engineers use every week, with measurable time savings and quality improvements.
Added new civil-specific capabilities to our AI agents, so they can work directly with the models and data our teams produce.
Built a library of documented, evaluated workflows that other teams can pick up and adapt.
Become the go-to person engineers call when they think, "There has to be a better way to do this."

Why Join Us

Real impact: your work goes straight into the maps that help infrastructure owners avoid utility strikes, delays, and safety risks on major projects.
An AI-native company: AI already sits at the core of how we read the subsurface. You will extend it to how we engineer and deliver.
A rare mix of disciplines: geophysics, civil engineering, BIM, and modern AI in one role, with a global team spanning the US, Israel, and beyond.
Room to shape, from the ground up, how a fast-growing company scales its engineering delivery with AI.
Close collaboration with field, mapping, and engineering experts who care about getting the underground right.

Our mission is to power the next era of underground exploration – saving time, money, lives, and the planet. We are focused, intentional, confident, and hard working. We solve big problems, but we are approachable, open-minded, and love hard questions.

You can learn more about us on our website or check out this short video.

Apply on our careers page, via Linkedin or send your resume to cara.partovich@exodigo.ai

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. Today, ServiceNow is the AI control tower for business reinvention. We're building an AI-native culture where technology and talent are unstoppable together. And we're just getting started.

Join us to put AI to work for people.

Job Description

The Role

Are you up for an exciting challenge? Picture yourself scaling and optimizing a cutting-edge Generative AI product that offers instant assistance to enterprise users. Ever wondered how to apply abstraction, scalability, and optimization to a dynamic, probabilistic, and generative conversational system? If so, we invite you to join our Conversation Engine team. At our company, you'll have the unique opportunity to work at the core of Moveworks Generative AI product. Your main focus will be scaling and optimizing it to meet the growing demands of the enterprise solution space. Take a look at our recent posts (Moveworks Live, Creator Studio) on Moveworks’s groundbreaking solutions for enterprise AI. As pioneers in enterprise AI, we don't follow a set formula for building the next solution. Instead, we encourage you to bring your innovative ideas and imagination to solve unsolved problems. You'll collaborate closely with machine learning experts and cross-functional teams, rapidly iterating over new ideas, and leveraging user behavior data to make informed decisions. Your challenge will be to scale and optimize our conversation engine to support hundreds of millions of users, across multiple chat channels and use cases, and enhance our end-to-end product infrastructure with the utmost engineering quality and robustness.

What You Get To Do In This Role

Construct an extensive product infrastructure, complete with user-friendly interfaces that empower engineers and configurators to effortlessly customize and optimize generative AI models. This includes collecting data and feedback, adapting to diverse enterprise use cases and business contexts, and delivering domain-specific conversational experiences.
Design scalable API abstractions for our conversation platform, which supports all popular chat clients (for example, MSTeams, Slack, and Web) and offers a neutral API for developing other parts of the engineering system.
Optimize the dialog engine to accommodate a wide range of conversational features, leveraging private domain knowledge unique to each enterprise customer in the cloud, and enable real-time multilingual translation. You will achieve this with minimal memory footprint, low latency, and streamlined development process for application engineers.
Champion the best practices for coding patterns, API design, scalability, robustness, and optimization. Foster a culture of excellence and continuous improvements among fellow engineers.
Provide comprehensive insights and visibility into the performance of our conversational AI product. This involves implementing a robust logging and tracing framework, user-friendly debugging and triaging tools, and automated metrics for efficient monitoring and analysis.
Collaborate closely with ML engineers, application engineers, product teams, and customer support teams to drive the development of new features and scalability initiatives.

Qualifications

To be successful in this role you have:

A strong foundation in computer science and software engineering, coupled with expertise in building scalable systems.
A deep understanding of clean, modular, and scalable API design. You have the ability to champion best coding practices and influence fellow engineers to uphold high standards of code quality and craftsmanship.
A passion for optimizing systems and improving performance. You are well-versed in tracing, logging, and metrics frameworks, and possess a systematic approach to quickly identify and resolve latency bottlenecks, race conditions, and throughput limitations.
The ability to independently research new requirements and develop innovative solutions. You thrive in an environment of fast-paced coding and execution, embracing rapid iterations to deliver results.
Strong communication skills to effectively articulate rationales and design approaches. You have a cross-functional awareness that enables you to collaborate seamlessly with various teams.
A bachelor's degree or higher in computer science or a related field, demonstrating your academic foundation in the field.
5+ years of professional development experience, specifically in building systems at scale.

added.title: Forward Deployed Engineer
added.description:
Plain is redefining customer support and customer success for the next generation of B2B companies. We’re building the fastest, most powerful platform to help companies move beyond reactive support and build meaningful customer relationships.

Some of the world’s most forward-thinking companies - like Cursor, Vercel, and Granola - trust Plain to unify all customer interactions, enable faster team collaboration, and supercharge their workflows with AI.

We have offices in SF and London. This role is hybrid with 3 days a week in our SF office. Because we work closely with our teammates in Europe, we start early, but you’ll find quiet afternoons for heads-down work.

Why this role is special

Our most strategic customers do not arrive through self-serve. They arrive with an existing support setup, a lot of context to migrate, and workflows that do not exist in Plain yet. Getting them live is genuine engineering work, and today that work lands on the core engineering team. It gets done, and it gets done well, but it moves the roadmap around more than we want it to.
That is the gap this role closes. You own that work end to end, which means customers get an engineer whose entire job is their problem, and the core team gets a clearer run at the product. The other half of the job is deciding which of that work should stop being bespoke and become product, so the same thing never gets built twice.

What you'll do

Work directly with customers to diagnose the problem, scope the fix, and ship it end to end.
Own the system design for customer deployments, trading off correctness, scale, and speed as the situation demands.
Explain the plan and the tradeoffs to whoever is in the room, engineer or not.
Work with Sales, CX, Product, and core Engineering to get what you learn into the roadmap.
Help define how the Forward Deployed function runs as it grows.

This is a great fit if you…

Have built and shipped full-stack products end to end. You are at home in modern frontend (React and TypeScript) and you write backend that holds up in production.
Prototype quickly and learn from real usage. You would rather put something in front of a customer and change it than get the design right on paper first.
Communicate exceptionally well. You can run a customer call, turn a vague ask into concrete scope, and write it up so nobody has to ask what was agreed.
Have strong product sense. You can separate what a customer asked for from what they actually need, you know which one-off work should turn into product and which should stay one-off, and you have the taste to decide whether it is worth building at all.
Own the outcome without much scaffolding. This is an IC role in an early-stage, ambiguous environment, and you do not wait for clean requirements before unblocking someone.
Stay calm when things get tense. Delays, bugs, and de-scoping conversations come with the job, and you can say yes to the reasonable asks while pushing back on the rest.

Our tech stack

We choose tools that empower both humans and AI:
Frontend: React and TypeScript
Backend: TypeScript and GraphQL
Cloud: AWS, Cloudflare, and multiple LLM providers
Tooling: GitHub Actions, Datadog, Terraform, and more

The stack keeps evolving with whatever works best.

This won't be the right role if you…

Want a heads-down role with no customer contact.
Have little patience for customer messiness.
Over-engineer, and chase perfection at the cost of speed.
Struggle to say no, or take every request at face value.
Only thrive with detailed specs and stable requirements.

added.description:
WHAT YOU DO AT AMD CHANGES EVERYTHING

At AMD, our mission is to build great products that accelerate next-generation computing experiences—from AI and data centers, to PCs, gaming and embedded systems. Grounded in a culture of innovation and collaboration, we believe real progress comes from bold ideas, human ingenuity and a shared passion to create something extraordinary. When you join AMD, you’ll discover the real differentiator is our culture. We push the limits of innovation to solve the world’s most important challenges—striving for execution excellence, while being direct, humble, collaborative, and inclusive of diverse perspectives. Join us as we shape the future of AI and beyond. Together, we advance your career.

The Role

We're looking for a Forward Deployed Research Engineer
to build, evaluate, and deploy cutting-edge AI systems that solve complex engineering challenges for enterprise customers.

This is not
a traditional Solutions Engineer or prompt engineering role. You'll combine deep software engineering, applied AI research, and customer engagement to develop production-ready AI systems using modern LLMs, reinforcement learning, agentic workflows, and post-training techniques.

The Person

You'll work directly with customers, researchers, and product teams to transform ambiguous engineering problems into scalable AI solutions. From rapid prototyping to production deployment, you'll help shape both customer success and the evolution of our AI platform.

What Makes This Role Unique

Build AI systems that solve real-world engineering problems—not proof-of-concepts.
Work across applied AI research, software engineering, and customer deployment.
Partner directly with enterprise engineering teams to define, build, and validate AI solutions.
Influence future AI products by translating customer challenges into reusable platform capabilities.
Own projects end-to-end—from technical discovery and experimentation through deployment and measurable impact.

Key Responsibilities

Partner with customer engineering teams to understand workflows, technical challenges, and opportunities for AI-driven automation.
Design, build, and deploy production-grade AI applications, LLM agents, and engineering automation solutions.
Develop evaluation frameworks, benchmarks, testing environments, and data pipelines to measure model quality and business impact.
Build and evaluate LLM post-training solutions, including supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, preference optimization, and reward modeling.
Diagnose and optimize AI system performance across models, data, infrastructure, orchestration, and tooling.
Collaborate with AI researchers to validate new models and techniques in production environments.
Present technical solutions, architecture, and implementation strategies to engineering leaders, customers, and executive stakeholders.
Transform recurring customer use cases into reusable AI infrastructure, frameworks, and platform capabilities.

Required Qualifications

Strong software engineering experience in Python and at least one systems language such as C++, Rust, C, TypeScript, CUDA, or HIP.
Proven experience building production AI or machine learning systems beyond prompt engineering or API integrations.
Hands-on experience with one or more of the following:
LLM post-training
Reinforcement Learning (RLHF, PPO, DPO, GRPO, or similar)
Preference Optimization
Reward Modeling
Model or Agent Evaluation
AI Training or Inference Infrastructure

Deep understanding of transformer-based LLMs, inference, fine-tuning, retrieval, evaluation, and agent architectures.
Experience designing reproducible evaluation frameworks using benchmarks, testing, and measurable performance metrics.
Strong systems thinking, debugging, and problem-solving skills.
Experience translating ambiguous technical requirements into scalable production solutions.
Ability to work directly with customers and technical stakeholders to drive solution design, implementation, and adoption.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills with engineers, researchers, customers, and executive leadership.

Experience training, fine-tuning, or post-training foundation models or open-source LLMs.
Experience with PyTorch, Hugging Face, JAX, TensorFlow, Ray, vLLM, or distributed AI infrastructure.
Experience building AI agents, retrieval systems, tool calling, workflow orchestration, or automated code generation.
Experience with GPU optimization, CUDA, distributed systems, or high-performance computing.
Background in forward-deployed engineering, applied AI research, customer engineering, or solutions architecture.
Demonstrated success delivering AI solutions from customer discovery through deployment with measurable business impact.

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Machine Learning, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience). Master's preferred; PhD is a plus for candidates with strong applied research or systems experience

added.title: Principal AI Engineer, Trust & Evaluation
added.description:
Who are we?

Equinix is the world’s digital infrastructure company®, shortening the path to connectivity to enable the innovations that enrich our work, life and planet.

A place where tech thinkers and future builders turn bold ideas into breakthrough experiences, we welcome your unique perspective.

Help us challenge assumptions, uncover bias, and remove barriers—because progress starts with fresh ideas. You’ll find belonging, purpose, and a team that welcomes you—because when you feel valued, you’re empowered to do your best work.

Job Summary

Sets the technical direction for the evaluation and trust capabilities of Equinix's GenAI platform, and designs, develops and deploys them. Builds platform features that let teams evaluate their agents at scale: golden datasets, synthetic test data, scoring with LLM-as-judge, and monitoring of agent quality in production. Designs and tests the trust controls that agents run on, including agent identity, access, guardrails and data boundaries. Leads the investigation of the hardest agent failures and fixes them in the platform. Serves as the hands-on technical lead of the Trust & Evaluation team, and partners with product, platform, security and governance leaders to turn ambiguous problems into robust, secure, observable and performant solutions.

Knowledge and Application Applies expert knowledge of software engineering practice and of LLM and agent concepts (prompting, retrieval, tool and function calling, orchestration, MCP). Has deep expertise in evaluation methods (code-based checks, LLM-as-judge, human review, golden datasets, regression suites) and evaluation statistics (sampling, variance across runs, agreement between reviewers). Has a deep understanding of AI security risks such as prompt injection and data leakage, and of identity concepts such as OAuth, token exchange and per-user access. Sets the standards and practices that the team and other teams follow, and keeps them current with industry research.

Complexity and Problem Solving Works on complex, open-ended problems that span teams, where the right approach is not yet known. Leads the investigation of the hardest agent failures (retrieval, tool call, prompt, model, data or infrastructure) and follows them until they are fixed. Decides which metrics reflect real quality and sets the bar for release. Makes architecture decisions with long-term impact on the platform, and resolves trade-offs among quality, cost, latency and security. Work is reviewed at design and milestone gates for results against long-term goals.

Collaboration and Interaction Partners with product, platform, security, legal and governance leaders, and with forward-deployed engineers and agent builders across the company. Turns the needs of agent builders into a platform roadmap. Explains results, risks and trade-offs to senior and non-technical stakeholders. Mentors engineers, raises the technical bar of the team, and leads through influence across teams.

Responsibilities

Evaluation platform (primary focus)

Own the architecture and roadmap for platform evaluation features, and build them: dataset creation and versioning, golden datasets, synthetic test data and reusable metric templates
Design and build the scoring approach for agents (code-based checks, LLM-as-judge, tool-call accuracy and grounding checks), and decide which methods apply where
Design and build human-review features that compare judge scores against human reviewers, and set the agreement level required before teams rely on a judge
Define how evaluations run at scale: before release, on every change to a prompt, model or tool, and on agents in production
Define the evaluation standard and playbooks that every agent release follows, so agent builders can evaluate their agents without specialist help
Keep results traceable to the agent, model, prompt and dataset versions tested, with a record of who approved each release, ready for audit

Trust and safety

Design the platform's trust architecture and lead its build: agent identity, per-user access to connected systems, tool permissions, guardrails and data boundaries
Lead adversarial testing and red-teaming (prompt injection, out-of-scope requests, data-boundary tests), and turn findings into fixes and regression tests
Partner with security and governance leaders to turn policy requirements into automated checks

Root-cause analysis and quality

Lead the investigation of the hardest agent failures and performance problems end to end, and follow them until the cause is fixed
Set the approach for test and performance tooling: end-to-end agent tests, load and latency tests, and failure diagnostics
Make sure production failures and user feedback become regression tests, so the same defect does not return

Quality and responsible practice

Write tested, reviewed and documented code, contribute to shared libraries and tooling, and review the team's designs and code
Make sure the team tests and builds to security, data-privacy and responsible-AI requirements

Qualifications

Required

7+ years in software, ML or platform engineering, including 3+ years building ML or LLM systems in production
Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, data science, mathematics or a related field, or equivalent experience
Expert Python, with solid habits: version control, testing, code review. Track record of designing backend services or platform features used by many teams
Track record of designing and leading the build of evaluation, testing or quality platforms for ML or LLM applications, used by many teams or at scale
Deep knowledge of LLM applications and agents (prompting, retrieval, tool calling) and how they fail, including tracing hard failures to their root cause through logs and traces
Deep knowledge of evaluation statistics (sampling, confidence intervals, variance across runs) and of measuring agreement between reviewers
Ability to write SQL and analyze results
Experience leading technical work across teams and influencing without direct authority
Clear written and verbal communication, including with senior and non-technical stakeholders

Nice to have

Experience with LLM evaluation and observability tools, and tracing standards such as OpenTelemetry
Experience with red-teaming or adversarial testing of LLM systems
Experience with identity and access (OAuth 2.0, OIDC, delegated access)
Experience with performance, load or test engineering
Experience with agent frameworks, MCP or A2A
Experience with Google Cloud (Vertex AI, GKE) and Kubernetes
Familiarity with AI risk frameworks (NIST AI RMF, ISO 42001)
Published research, patents, talks or open-source contributions in evaluation or AI safety
MS or PhD in a related field

What success looks like

The evaluation and trust roadmap is delivered on schedule, with tests and documentation
Teams can evaluate their agents on the platform without specialist help
Every agent release carries an evaluation record with criteria, results, open defects and approver
Judge scores agree with human reviewers, and teams use them to make release decisions
Trust controls are enforced by the platform, covered by automated tests, and pass security and governance reviews
Defects found in evaluation become regression tests, and the same defect does not return
Engineers on the team grow in scope and skill, and the team's standards are adopted by other teams across Equinix

Decagon is the leading conversational AI platform empowering every brand to deliver concierge customer experiences.

Decagon’s Data Science team supports the core agent platform within EPD, our Engineering, Research, Product, and Design organization. Hands-on experience building, evaluating, or monitoring AI agents or other LLM-powered products
Experience using AI tools in your own data science work to write and debug code, explore data, or automate recurring analyses, and independently validating the results.

At Palo Alto Networks®, we’re united by a shared mission—to protect our digital way of life. We thrive at the intersection of innovation and impact, solving real-world problems with cutting-edge technology and bold thinking. Here, everyone has a voice, and every idea counts. If you’re ready to do the most meaningful work of your career alongside people who are just as passionate as you are, you’re in the right place.

added.description:
Opportunity

Offerwall by Unity is a leading mobile advertising and monetization platform that empowers game developers to maximize revenue and engage users through rewarded experiences. For over a decade, we've connected millions of players with offers that provide tangible in-app value, and we're now building the next generation of that product.

Rewarded advertising attracts fraud. Every conversion attempt on Offerwall and the Unity Rewards app is scored in real time by our fraud detection stack: a prediction service, an online feature store, streaming and batch feature pipelines, and a rules engine that decides what gets paid out. When fraud gets through, money leaks from our advertisers and our business.

We're seeking a Machine Learning Engineer to own the ML side of Offerwall fraud prevention. You'll take our real-time anomaly detection and device risk models from development into production, build the labeled fraud dataset and evaluation methodology the team measures itself against, and modernize how we train, serve, and monitor models. You'll work closely with data engineering, backend, and product partners who own the systems your models plug into.

This is a hands-on role with real scope. You'll be one of a small group of engineers responsible for fraud ML end to end, and you'll have a direct line from the models you ship to dollars saved.

What You'll Be Doing

Ship Fraud Models to Production: Take our real-time anomaly detection and device risk models from development to production, so their output drives payout and blocking decisions.
Build the Ground Truth: Create and maintain a golden labeled fraud dataset, and define the evaluation methodology and baseline fraud-efficacy metrics the team uses to judge every model and rule change.
Own Features End to End: Design and evolve the streaming and batch features that feed our Redis online feature store, partnering with data engineering on freshness, correctness, and lineage.
Modernize ML Infrastructure: Plan and drive the evolution of our training and serving stack, including evaluating a move from SageMaker to Kubeflow and KServe, with attention to latency on the real-time scoring path.
Detect New Fraud Patterns: Investigate fraud spikes, analyze user and device behavior, and turn findings into new detection signals, features, and models.
Operate & Document: Monitor model and feature health in production, write runbooks and data lineage docs, and participate in on-call for the fraud detection stack.

What We're Looking For

Production ML Experience: Several years building ML models and taking them all the way to production, including deployment, monitoring, and iteration after launch.
Fraud, Risk, or Anomaly Detection: Hands-on experience with fraud detection, abuse prevention, risk scoring, or anomaly detection, including working with sparse, noisy, or adversarial labels.
Real-time Serving & Feature Engineering: Experience with low-latency model serving and online/offline feature pipelines (for example Redis or another online feature store, Kafka or similar streaming, Airflow).
Evaluation Rigor: Ability to build labeled datasets from imperfect signals and design evaluation methods that hold up when fraud patterns shift.
Core Technologies: Strong Python and SQL. Working knowledge of a cloud ML platform such as AWS SageMaker, Kubeflow, or KServe.
Ownership & Collaboration: You take ambiguous problems to shipped outcomes with limited oversight, write things down, and work well with backend, data, and product partners. You use AI coding tools to move faster.

You might also have

Experience with ad fraud, install/attribution fraud, or fraud in rewarded or incentivized advertising.
Experience with unsupervised or semi-supervised detection methods such as autoencoders, isolation forests, or graph-based approaches to device and user linking.
Experience migrating ML serving between platforms, or building MLOps tooling on Kubernetes.
Background in mobile ad tech, mobile games, or app monetization.

Description

The Amazon Center for Quantum Computing (CQC) is seeking an Applied Scientist to research and design superconducting qubit devices and circuit elements for scalable quantum processors. You will design qubits, couplers, resonators, and supporting microwave circuitry; develop and validate electromagnetic and Hamiltonian models of those devices; and carry designs from concept through simulation, layout, design review, and fabrication handoff. You will evaluate alternative processor architectures and packaging approaches against quantitative scaling metrics, and work closely with the co-located processor design team so that what we learn about future systems improves the systems being built today.

Key job responsibilities

Design superconducting quantum devices — qubits, couplers, readout and Purcell circuitry, and supporting microwave elements — for processor architectures beyond the current generation
Develop, validate, and document electromagnetic and circuit-Hamiltonian models of these devices, and deliver design artifacts through the organization's design-request and design-review processes
Collaborate with fabrication, measurement, packaging, and control-electronics colleagues to close the loop between design predictions and measured devices
Contribute to design-automation and simulation workflows used across the physical design teams
Present results internally and, where appropriate, publish in peer-reviewed venues

About The Team

The Enabling Technologies team develops technologies and relationships facilitating scaling, including alternative quantum processor architectures, superconducting qubit device packaging, and cryogenic control device electronics. We work alongside a co-located quantum processor design team focused on current-generation devices; the two teams share design and review processes, and moving ideas between them is an explicit part of our charter.

3+ years of building models for business application experience
Experience in patents or publications at top-tier peer-reviewed conferences or journals
Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language
Experience in any of the following areas: algorithms and data structures, parsing, numerical optimization, data mining, parallel and distributed computing, high-performance computing

Experience using Unix/Linux

About Baseten

Baseten powers mission-critical inference for the world's most dynamic AI companies, like Cursor, Notion, OpenEvidence, Abridge, Clay, Gamma, and Writer. By uniting applied AI research, flexible infrastructure, and seamless developer tooling, we enable companies operating at the frontier of AI to bring cutting-edge models into production. We're growing quickly and recently raised our $1.5B Series F, led by Altimeter Capital, Conviction Partners, and Spark Capital. Join us and help build the platform engineers turn to ship AI products.

THE ROLE

As the Revenue Strategy & Operations Manager for Baseten’s AI Natives, AI Strategics, and Labs segments, you’ll be the day-to-day RevOps partner to the leaders who run them: our Sales Leaders across AI Natives & Strategics and our Head of Sales for Labs. You’ll give them the analysis and operating support to run their segments, and turn their priorities into the plans, targets, and operating cadence the segments run on.

These segments cover some of Baseten’s largest and fastest-growing customers. Revenue is consumption-based, so growth comes from workloads scaling inside existing accounts as much as from new logos, and planning, forecasting, and pipeline management have to reflect that. You’ll sit on the Revenue Strategy & Operations team and work closely with Finance, Comp, Enablement, Territory Ops, GTM Engineering, and Sales leadership. You’ll own the segments’ numbers, the reviews that inspect them, and the processes and systems that keep them reliable.

What You'll Work On

Segment planning: Turn segment leaders’ priorities into joint plans with clear decisions, owners, and deadlines, and track them to completion.
Operating cadence: Run segment MBRs, QBRs, and forecast reviews so leaders understand the business, decisions get made, and every follow-up has an owner.
Planning and targets: Build the models behind annual and in-year planning for the segments: headcount, quota, and pipeline targets.
Pipeline and forecasting: Inspect deals, pressure-test commits, and surface risk early in a business where revenue moves with customer usage.
Segment analytics: Own funnel and consumption analytics, and build analytics products with GTM Engineering that flag risks and opportunities early.
Process and systems: Build the segments’ sales processes into our systems and get segment managers onboarded onto them.

Responsibilities

Business partnership
Partner with our Heads of Sales for AI Natives and Labs as the RevOps lead for their segments
Bring segment leaders the analysis they need to decide where to focus and invest
Translate segment strategy into joint plans with clear decisions, owners, and deadlines, and track them to completion
Run segment MBRs and QBRs that give leaders an accurate, shared view of the business, drive decisions, and assign owners

Planning, targets, and capacity
Run the annual and in-year planning process for the segments
Build the capacity, quota, and pipeline models behind segment targets, in partnership with the VP of RevOps and Finance
Work with the Comp team to implement segment compensation plans and track their impact

Pipeline, forecasting, and analytics
Run segment forecast reviews: inspect deals, pressure-test commits, and surface risks early
Own segment funnel analytics: stage conversion, win rates, new logos, activations, renewals, consumption trends, and product mix
Build segment analytics products with GTM Engineering that surface risks and opportunities early and often

Operations and process
Build the segments’ sales processes into our systems (Salesforce and the wider GTM stack)
Partner with Enablement to onboard segment managers onto seller motions and tools

Qualifications

3 to 5 years in Revenue Operations, Sales Strategy & Operations, BizOps, FP&A, or management consulting, ideally including time partnering directly with sales leaders
Experience running forecast and business review cadences (weekly forecast calls, MBRs, QBRs) for a sales segment or region
Hands-on experience supporting annual planning: building capacity, quota, or pipeline coverage models
Strong analytical skills: you build your own models in spreadsheets and pull your own data from Salesforce, BI Tools, or directly from a data warehouse. You write SQL and don’t just rely on Claude.
Working knowledge of Salesforce and sales process design (stages, exit criteria, forecast categories)
Clear, structured communication: you turn analysis into a clear recommendation and present it to sales leaders
Comfortable with ambiguity and pace; you build the process rather than wait for one

NICE TO HAVE

Experience with consumption or usage-based revenue (cloud, API, or infrastructure businesses)
Experience supporting enterprise or strategic segments with large, concentrated customers
Experience implementing or administering sales compensation plans
Exposure to AI/ML infrastructure or developer-focused products

Exposure to a variety of ML startups, offering unparalleled learning and networking opportunities.

About Gusto

At Gusto, we're on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. With teams in Denver, San Francisco, and New York, we support more than 500,000 small businesses nationwide and are building a workplace that reflects the people we serve.

All full-time employees receive competitive base pay, benefits, and equity (RSUs) — because everyone who helps build Gusto should share in its success. Offer amounts are determined by role, level, and location. Learn more about our Total Rewards philosophy.

AI is a fundamental part of how work gets done at Gusto. We expect all team members to actively engage with AI tools relevant to their role and grow their fluency as the technology evolves. AI experience requirements vary by role and will be assessed during the interview process.

About The Role

As a Staff Machine Learning Platform Engineer, you will work closely with AI/ML engineers to rapidly build, deploy, and iterate high-quality ML/AI infrastructure solutions at scale, ensuring both reliability and effectiveness. Your deep expertise in the machine learning

Model development cycle, along with a strong understanding of data pipelines and data infrastructure will be crucial in developing a dependable and scalable ML/AI infrastructure for all of Gusto to rely on.

The ideal candidate is passionate about developing software, developing and documenting optimal processes, working with data, and understanding the needs of end users. A strong grasp of ML and data infrastructure is essential, as you will work with stakeholders to build efficient solutions to help our partners scale x times better.

Here’s What You’ll Do Day-to-day

Build core components of our ML and AI Platform technical roadmap to design and build MLOps solutions with automated pipelines and standardized processes to build, deploy, run, monitor, debug, and retrain ML and AI Models.
Develop, maintain, and enhance frameworks for machine learning model development and deployment.
Collaborate with the ML/AI builders and application owners to determine business requirements and SLAs for API-enabled services.
Develop, maintain, and enhance infrastructure supporting machine learning services.
Support the development of new patterns for the deployment of machine learning models with CI/CD pipelines and automated testing.
Apply AI tools as a regular part of your engineering workflow, and bring an AI-native lens to engineering and product decisions: identify where AI can reduce effort, simplify complex workflows, and surface proactive guidance.
Adopt the latest best practices for using AI technologies across all aspects of technical development

Here’s What We’re Looking For

At least 8+ years of software engineering experience (Python, Ruby or Java).
Demonstrated experience designing and developing infrastructure and platform services for machine learning lifecycle, such as feature stores, model development, deployment, and observability tools and solutions.
Experience with at least one of the major cloud platforms (AWS preferred but not required).
Curiosity and experimentation with emerging AI frameworks, applying and sharing best practices to evaluate and scale AI use safely across teams

added.title: Principal Solution Architect, Commercialization and Corporate Systems
added.description:
Revolution Medicines is a global, commercial-state oncology company dedicated to discovering, developing and delivering innovative medicines for patients with RAS-addicted cancers. Leveraging its differentiated RAS(ON) tri-complex inhibitor platform, the company is advancing a broad, integrated portfolio of oral RAS(ON) inhibitors designed to directly target the active, cancer-driving state of RAS. Founded on rigorous scientific inquiry and a willingness to challenge long-held assumptions, Revolution Medicines is committed to changing the trajectory of disease for patients with RAS-addicted cancers worldwide.

Our people are united by a shared way of working: follow the science, challenge assumptions, act with urgency and hold ourselves to a high standard of rigor—all in service of patients.

The Opportunity:

Revolution Medicines is seeking a Principal Solutions Architect to lead integrated technology design across Commercial, Medical Affairs and General & Administrative (G&A) functions. This leader will shape architecture across the evolving business application portfolio, connecting processes, data and platforms to support commercialization, global expansion and efficient operations. The role will guide solution decisions from business intake through implementation and operational readiness, working closely with functional leaders, Information Technology (IT), control owners and delivery partners. This is a Director-level individual contributor role with technical leadership responsibilities across cross-functional teams and external partners.

Responsibilities:

Define target architecture and inform investment roadmaps across current and future Commercial, Medical Affairs and G&A capabilities, translating business strategy into integrated solutions that support product launches, international expansion and enterprise growth.
Partner with business and technology leaders to shape requests, clarify outcomes and dependencies, assess options, and recommend solutions based on business value, risk, scalability and total cost of ownership.
Provide architecture leadership across the G&A portfolio, including Finance, Human Resources, Procurement, Legal, corporate services and enterprise operations. Connect workflows across these functions and with Commercialization, Supply Chain, and other business areas, extending architecture patterns as new business capabilities emerge.
Provide architecture leadership for critical cross-platform integrations, new capabilities and key technology decisions across Commercial and Medical systems, partnering with Medical, Omnichannel, Field and Data Solutions leads who own solution design within their respective areas. Assess enterprise platform scalability, including enterprise resource planning (ERP), for growth in legal entities, products, users and transaction volumes. Guide global templates and local requirements for language, currency, tax, statutory reporting and business practices.
Architect connected planning, forecasting and external partner ecosystems as business needs evolve. Examples include linking commercial and financial plans with supply operations and integrating third-party logistics (3PL) providers, distributors and manufacturing partners.
Evaluate artificial intelligence (AI), automation and emerging technologies against business needs. Reuse existing enterprise tools where suitable and define integration, data access, human oversight and measurable outcomes for new capabilities.
Inform buy-versus-build recommendations, assessing how advances in AI change the feasibility, speed and cost of developing and maintaining custom solutions relative to commercial platforms, while considering security, compliance, integration, scalability and long-term support.
Define reusable application, data and integration patterns using application programming interfaces (APIs), integration platforms and events. Establish authoritative data sources, master data ownership, reconciliation and exception handling with the relevant domain owners.
Partner with enterprise Data teams to design reliable information flows, consistent business definitions and reporting dependencies across operational systems, analytics and decision support.
Establish design standards and architecture reviews. Document decisions, system boundaries and dependencies, and resolve cross-platform trade-offs while keeping delivery teams accountable for implementation quality.
Provide technical leadership from discovery and vendor selection through design, implementation, testing, deployment and operational acceptance. Define performance, availability, recovery and support requirements early in the lifecycle.
Design for global delivery and support, with clear ownership, monitoring, knowledge transfer and handoffs across time zones. Ensure solutions transition to internal teams and managed service providers with agreed readiness criteria.
Partner with Security, Quality, Privacy, Finance and control owners to embed applicable Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX), Good Practice (GxP), General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and local requirements into designs, including access, segregation of duties, validation, audit trails and retention.
Identify opportunities to simplify workflows, consolidate overlapping systems and reduce integration and support costs. Define the growth, risk and performance thresholds that trigger a different platform or operating approach.

Partner with platform owners, domain specialists, engineers and architects across internal and external teams to develop solution designs and integrations across systems, drawing on their expertise while maintaining overall architectural coherence. Challenge designs constructively, communicate recommendations to senior leaders, and ensure vendor solutions meet RevMed architecture standards and agreed commercial scope.

Required Skills, Experience and Education:

Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Information Systems, Engineering or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
12+ years of progressive technology experience, including 5+ years in solution architecture or comparable technical leadership across complex enterprise programs.
Experience in life sciences or another regulated industry is required; biotech or pharmaceutical experience is highly preferred.
Demonstrated architecture experience spanning Commercial or Medical platforms and enterprise G&A systems, with depth in one or more domains and the ability to lead design decisions across the broader portfolio.
Demonstrated ability to anticipate technology shifts and apply AI and automation to solution design and delivery, challenging established approaches and introducing practical new ways of working that improve speed, quality and business outcomes.
Strong experience with cloud and software-as-a-service platforms, integration architecture, enterprise data flows, security and nonfunctional requirements such as performance, reliability and recovery.
Experience translating business requirements into architecture options, roadmaps and technical designs, and guiding delivery through implementation and transition to support.
Working knowledge of applicable SOX controls, regulated-system lifecycle practices, privacy and data protection requirements, and experience partnering with the accountable specialists to implement controls.
Ability to influence senior stakeholders, explain technical trade-offs in business terms, resolve competing priorities and lead internal and partner teams without relying on direct reporting authority.

Preferred Skills:

Experience supporting oncology commercialization, multiple product launches, new legal entities or expansion across the United States, Europe and Asia Pacific.
Experience architecting solutions across enterprise platforms such as Veeva CRM, Oracle NetSuite, SAP, Workday, Ironclad Contract Lifecycle Management, Salesforce Marketing Cloud and Databricks, or comparable platforms. Depth in one or more of these ecosystems, combined with experience integrating solutions across business functions, is preferred.
Experience with external commercial, distribution or manufacturing integrations, master data management, or regulated content and review workflows.
Practical experience deploying AI or automation with enterprise controls, and improving platform reuse, delivery speed or total cost of ownership.
Enterprise or solution architecture certification, or equivalent demonstrated architecture practice.

LLM orchestration:

AI evaluation and safety:
Implement automated evaluation frameworks, regression testing, guardrails, hallucination detection and safety mechanisms suitable for healthcare applications.
Classical machine learning:
Develop, train, validate and deploy predictive ML models using statistical analysis and modern ML frameworks.
Production AI infrastructure:
Build reliable model-serving systems, inference pipelines, observability, monitoring and scalable AI services.
Agentic workflows:
Develop context-aware AI workflows with structured tool use, state management, memory and robust failure handling.

You'll be expected to write substantial production code, make architectural decisions and own your systems beyond initial deployment.
What we're looking for

Strong hands-on experience developing and operating production AI/ML systems.
Practical expertise with LLM applications, RAG, embeddings, vector databases and orchestration frameworks.
Strong Python engineering skills and experience with PyTorch, scikit-learn or comparable ML frameworks.

Experience designing automated LLM evaluation, regression testing and production safety controls.
Experience with cloud platforms, APIs, distributed systems, CI/CD and production monitoring.
The ability to work independently, solve complex technical problems and deliver reliable systems in a startup environment.

You understand that successful AI engineering is about more than prompts and prototypes. It requires rigorous experimentation, measurable evaluations, reliable deployment and ongoing ownership.
Above all, you want to build meaningful AI products used in the real world.

Meaningful healthcare impact:
Build technology that supports real patients and care teams.
Technical ownership:
Influence foundational AI architecture and personally deliver core production systems.
Modern AI stack:
Work with frontier models, open-weight models, retrieval, agentic systems and classical ML.

Share in the long-term value you help create.

Work from the greater Salt Lake City area, with just 1–2 days per week in Lehi.

added.title: Forward Deployed Engineer, Applied ML and Data
added.description:
About The Role

The Forward Deployed Engineer embeds with Hopper's partners, some of the world's largest banks, airlines and travel companies, to bring our AI into their business end to end: getting the data, building and tuning the models, and taking them to production. You will lead data and modelling on site as part of a small forward-deployed team, acting as the bridge between partners and Research. What makes the role distinctive is that the data that matters lives inside partners' own systems, so you make it usable, securely, and turn each deployment into reusable tooling that makes the next partner faster.

What would your day-to-day look like

Work on site with partner teams to connect to their systems, including on-premise and legacy platforms, and build secure, reliable data feeds.
Map messy, inconsistent commercial data from many sources into one clean model.
Build and run pipelines for large historical and near-real-time datasets, with monitoring and data quality checks.
Meet partners' security, privacy and IT review requirements, taking only the data the product needs.
Design, train and evaluate production ML models for a high-volume commercial use case, choosing the right approach and being clear about the trade-offs.
Build the evaluation and measurement that show whether the models are good enough, and where they aren't.
Build low-latency, high-throughput services that serve the models in production.
Design how the system decides what to answer and how, and how it improves from real usage.
Own reliability, cost and performance once the system is live.
Partner directly with technology and business teams, from first conversations to go-live.
Collaborate with Research and Product, feeding back what you learn in the field.
Turn each deployment into reusable tooling so the next partner goes faster.

An ideal candidate has

5+ years building and shipping production ML systems end to end, covering data, modelling, serving and monitoring, which you will apply to a high-volume commercial use case from day one.
Strong data engineering experience, having built and kept running pipelines over large, messy datasets, which you will use to turn partner data into one clean model.
Experience integrating with systems you don't control, such as enterprise, on-premise or legacy platforms, and working through a customer's security and IT review, so you can get partner data flowing securely.
Experience building and running services that handle thousands of requests per second at sub-second response times, which you will use to serve models in production.
Travel industry experience (airlines, hotels, OTAs, metasearch or travel technology) working with availability, rates, schedules and inventory, and the systems behind them such as GDS, NDC and airline and hotel reservation systems, so you can read partner data quickly and spot what matters.
Sound judgment on modelling trade-offs and the ability to explain them to non-technical partners, which you will use to guide partner teams through decisions from first conversations to go-live.
At least two deployments embedded with an enterprise customer, working inside their systems, data controls and security reviews, so you are ready to lead data and modelling on site.
Willingness to travel and spend multi-week stretches on site with partner teams.
Bonus: experience in both airline and hotel data, or in another high-volume marketplace (e-commerce, ad tech, fintech) as well as travel, to bring patterns from other verticals to each deployment.
Bonus: forecasting, estimation or recommendation models in production, and experience working alongside a research team to turn their methods into results at a customer.
Bonus: forward-deployed, solutions or integration engineering experience at an enterprise software or data company, or an advanced degree in computer science, statistics or a related field.

Well-funded and proven startup with large ambitions, competitive salary and the upsides of pre-IPO equity packages
Unlimited PTO
Carrot Cash travel stipend
Access to co-working space on demand through FlexDesk AND Work-from-home stipend
Please ask us about our very generous parental leave, much above industry standards!
Entrepreneurial culture where pushing limits and taking risks is everyday business
Open communication with management and company leadership
Small, dynamic teams = massive impact
100% employer paid Medical, Dental and Vision coverage for employees

DCA/ FSA and access to 401k plan

About Hopper

At Hopper, we’re building the leading travel technology platform in the world, and we’re doing it by solving real problems for real travelers globally. Our Hopper consumer booking platforms and HTS (Hopper Technology Solutions), our B2B business, work together to give travelers something the industry has never reliably offered: transparency, flexibility, and real savings on every trip. We combine massive amounts of data and AI with proprietary fintech products to make that happen, not just another booking engine, but a fundamentally better way to plan and experience travel for our customers and our partners. We are proof that better-for-the-customer and better-for-the-business can be one in the same

And we’re continuing to grow fast! The Hopper app has been downloaded over 120 million times, with 70% of our users being Gen Z and Millennials, next-generation travelers. Today, our biggest opportunity is powering travel fintech, commerce, and loyalty for some of the biggest brands in the industry. Our first HTS partnership with Capital One helped launch a dedicated travel portal for a major financial brand’s cardholders, and we’ve since expanded across some of the biggest names in travel and banking, including Air Canada, Uber, Royal Bank of Canada (RBC), and Nubank, powering everything from a single fintech integration to a full end-to-end travel loyalty portal.

That’s our trajectory: we started as a small, disruptive app within the travel space, and now we’re the engine under the hood powering how Travel Tech works.

Billions of dollars in travel and travel fintech move through Hopper and HTS every year.

added.description:
About Quantiphi:

Quantiphi is an award-winning, AI-First global digital engineering company that helps the world’s leading Fortune 1000 organizations transform bold ideas into measurable business impact. We go beyond building innovative AI technologies—we solve the problems that matter most to our clients.

Since our founding in 2013, Quantiphi has built a proven track record of turning complex challenges into meaningful outcomes across industries.

Headquartered in Boston, with more than 4,000 professionals worldwide, we partner with global enterprises to deliver large-scale digital, cloud, and AI-driven transformation. #SolvingWhatMatters

We are an Elite and Premier partner to Google Cloud, AWS, NVIDIA, Snowflake, and other leading technology platforms, and our work has been recognized across the industry, including:
21 Google Cloud Partner of the Year awards in the past 10 years
3 AWS AI/ML Partner of the Year awards
3 NVIDIA Partner of the Year awards
3 Snowflake Partner of the Year awards
Rated Leaders by Gartner, Forrester, IDC, ISG, Everest Group and other leading analyst firms

Quantiphi delivers First-in-class AI solutions across Life Sciences, Healthcare, Banking, Financial Services, CPG, Manufacturing, Energy, High-Tech, Telecommunications, etc., powered by cutting-edge Generative AI and Agentic AI accelerators.

We are also proud to be certified as a Great Place to Work
—reflecting our commitment to our people and our culture.

For more details, visit: Website or LinkedIn Page

Job Description:

We are seeking a highly skilled and motivated Machine Learning Engineer to join our AI/ML team. You will join a team that delivers AI agents and models into production for industrial use cases. You will own the path from experiment to production: fine-tuning, evaluation, inference optimization and benchmarking.

Key Responsibilities:

Model fine-tuning and evaluation

Fine-tune Nemotron, Gemma, or any other open-source models using techniques such as LoRA, QLoRA, RLHF, DPO, and SFT (Supervised Fine-Tuning), for tasks such as tool calling, RAG and domain-specific responses.
Build data pipelines for cleaning, curation, synthetic data generation, and train, validation and golden test sets.
Conduct prompt engineering and prompt tuning to optimize LLM/SLM agent behavior for specific use cases
Build evaluation frameworks covering function-calling accuracy, retrieval precision, task benchmarks and the accuracy-versus-latency trade-off.
Iterate on agent performance through systematic experimentation and hyperparameter optimization

Data Transformation & ML Modeling

Develop and maintain end-to-end data transformation pipelines for preparing training datasets, including data cleaning, augmentation, tokenization, and formatting
Design ML models and training architectures aligned with agent task objectives
Curate and manage high-quality instruction-tuning and RLHF datasets for agent training
Apply data-centric AI methodologies to improve model quality through better data rather than solely model changes
Build and validate benchmarks and evaluation datasets to track model improvements

GPU & Inference optimization, Edge Deployment

Architect and implement ML model deployment pipelines for edge environments (IoT devices, embedded systems, on-premise hardware)
Profile and optimize LLM inference for TTFT, end-to-end latency, throughput and GPU memory.
Tune vLLM and TensorRT-LLM deployments, including prefix caching, KV-cache configuration, attention backends, batching and quantization (FP8 / FP4 / NVFP4).
Optimize for NVIDIA GPUs and edge platforms (Blackwell-based, e.g., Jetson Thor), working within memory-bandwidth and hardware-feature constraints.
Address latency, memory, and compute constraints for real-time inference on edge devices
Apply knowledge distillation, pruning, and quantization techniques to reduce model size while maintaining performance
Run load, concurrency and accuracy regression tests every release cycle, and document what worked and what did not.
Collaborate with hardware and platform teams to ensure seamless integration of AI models into edge products

Required Skills & Qualifications:

Core technical skills (must-have)

LLM fine-tuning: Hands-on experience with SFT and parameter-efficient methods (LoRA / QLoRA), plus preference optimization (e.g., DPO) where relevant. You should have taken fine-tuned models from experiment to production.
ML stack: Strong Python, PyTorch and the Hugging Face ecosystem (Transformers, PEFT, TRL, Accelerate).
LLM inference and serving: Practical experience with vLLM, TensorRT-LLM or similar. This includes prefix caching, KV-cache configuration, batching, attention backends and quantization (FP8 / FP4 / NVFP4).
GPU architecture and profiling: CUDA fundamentals, Nsight or similar profilers, and the ability to diagnose memory, bandwidth and compute bottlenecks.
Performance benchmarking: Ability to run load, concurrency and accuracy regression tests. You should measure TTFT, end-to-end latency and throughput, and weigh the accuracy-versus-latency trade-off.
Evaluation design: Building benchmarks and golden datasets for LLMs and agents. Metrics include function-calling accuracy, retrieval precision and task success rate.
Data pipelines: Data curation, transformation, synthetic data generation, and train / validation / test splits.
Deployment and infrastructure: Docker, Kubernetes and Linux-based deployments, with familiarity with cloud or on-prem GPU environments.

Customer-facing and delivery skills (must-have)

Able to present benchmark results and recommendations to technical and business stakeholders, and to translate customer outcomes into model and infrastructure requirements.
Able to write technical documentation and operational guidance for handover, and to turn configurations and learnings into reusable accelerators.
Able to work with architects and other senior technical leads on design and best practices.
Able to coordinate with SME’s on roadmap, support and issue escalation.
Strong communication skills and comfort working embedded with customers.

Nice-to-have

Direct experience with NVIDIA Nemotron, NeMo, NIM or NeMo Guardrails.
Experience with edge NVIDIA platforms (Jetson-class) and their constraints, such as memory bandwidth and missing hardware features.
RAG, agentic frameworks (LangChain, LlamaIndex, AutoGen) and tool / function calling.
NL-to-SQL or small language model (SLM) evaluation.
Distributed training (DeepSpeed, FSDP), custom kernels, and experiment tracking (MLflow, W&B).
Async and non-blocking service design (e.g., FastAPI, asyncio) for LLM applications.
Open-source contributions, publications or talks.

What’s in it for YOU at Quantiphi?

Join one of the world’s fastest-growing AI-first digital engineering companies and make a real impact at scale.
Lead and collaborate with a high-energy team of talented, driven individuals solving complex, meaningful challenges.
Work with Fortune 500 companies and disruptive innovators in a research-driven environment with 60+ patents.
Stay ahead of the curve by gaining hands-on experience with cutting-edge AI, ML, data, and cloud technologies while continuously upskilling.

Job Title : Sr AI Engineer/Architect
Job Location: Atlanta, GA

The role

You will be the senior hands-on AI builder in the US, turning client conversations into working agents within days and production systems within weeks. You sit between presales and delivery: you design the architecture, build the proof of concept, demo it to client executives, and then lead the offshore engineering team that takes it to production.
This is a builder-architect role, not a slideware role. Expect to write code most weeks, stand in front of CIOs and AI committees most months, and own the technical quality of what Elixir ships to US clients.
Key responsibilities

Agentic AI solution design and build

Design and build multi-agent systems using LLMs (Claude, GPT, Gemini, Llama, Mistral), tool use, MCP and agent orchestration frameworks.
Build retrieval pipelines — RAG, GraphRAG and agentic RAG — with chunking strategies, embeddings, hybrid search, re-ranking and knowledge graphs.
Build conversational and voice AI assistants — chat and real-time voice — integrated with ITSM, ERP, HR and knowledge systems.
Build hardened, reusable agents for common enterprise needs — e.g. IDoc remediation, role and access recommendation, supply chain and inventory agents.

SAP and enterprise integration

Integrate agents with SAP ECC and S/4HANA (BAPIs, IDocs, OData, SAP BTP, Joule) and other enterprise systems (Oracle, JDE, ServiceNow, Salesforce, SharePoint).
Architect AI-assisted data pipelines on Snowflake or Databricks — mapping, cleansing, reconciliation and audit — for large-scale data migration.

Presales, POCs and client leadership

Turn a client pain point into a working demo fast — often a zero-dollar POC tied to outcome-based pricing.
Present architectures and live demos to client CIOs, CISOs, auditors and AI steering committees.
Support RFP responses with solution architecture, effort estimates and technical risk assessment.

Governance, security and production readiness

Apply responsible AI practices: guardrails, evaluation, observability, prompt and model versioning, and audit trails.
Design for regulated environments — SOX, HIPAA, segregation-of-duties controls, and FedRAMP / IL5 where required.
Own LLMOps: evaluation harnesses, cost and latency tuning, monitoring and model upgrades.

Required qualifications

Contribute to the AI Center of Excellence: reference architectures, reusable accelerators, client demo sandbox.
10+ years in software, data or ML engineering, including experience building production AI/ML systems and hands-on with LLMs and generative AI.
Shipped at least one agentic or LLM-powered application to production for an enterprise client — not only a prototype.
Strong Python; working knowledge of TypeScript/Node for agent front ends and APIs.
Hands-on with LLM APIs (Anthropic Claude, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Bedrock or Vertex), function/tool calling, MCP, RAG, GraphRAG, vector databases (pgvector, Pinecone, Weaviate or similar) and graph databases (Neo4j or similar).
Experience with at least one agent framework — LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, Claude Agent SDK, Semantic Kernel or equivalent.
Cloud-native delivery on AWS, Azure or GCP: containers, CI/CD, serverless, secrets and identity management.
Data engineering fundamentals: SQL, ETL/ELT, and a modern data platform such as Snowflake or Databricks.
Comfortable presenting to C-level and technical audiences, and writing clear architecture documents.

Preferred qualifications

Advanced retrieval — GraphRAG (e.g. Microsoft GraphRAG, LlamaIndex property graphs), knowledge-graph construction, entity extraction and ontology design.
Fine-tuning and serving open-weight models — LoRA / PEFT, vLLM, Ollama, quantization.
LLMOps and evaluation — LangSmith, Arize, Weights & Biases, Ragas, guardrail frameworks, red-teaming.
SAP integration experience — S/4HANA, ECC, BTP, IDocs/BAPIs, GRC/security roles, or SAP Joule and Business AI.
Regulated delivery: SOX, HIPAA, life sciences GxP, or FedRAMP / IL5 environments.
Domain depth in manufacturing, automotive, healthcare, financial services, or energy.
AI-driven quality engineering and test automation.
Experience leading distributed onshore/offshore teams in a consulting or services firm.

Company Overview:

Abiologics, Inc. is a privately held, early-stage biotechnology company on a mission to make biology better through an innovative therapeutic modality. We are pioneering the development of SynteinsTM, a transformational class of macromolecular medicines unlocked by novel synthetic and computational technologies. Abiologics is actively seeking exceptional molecular scientists who are passionate about driving therapeutic modality innovation in biotechnology.

Abiologics was founded in Flagship Pioneering’s venture creation engine, where companies such as Moderna Therapeutics (NASDAQ: MRNA) and Generate Biomedicines were conceived and created. Since Flagship’s founding in 2000, the firm has originated and fostered the development of more than 100 scientific ventures resulting in more than 500 issued patents and more than 50 clinical trials for novel therapeutic agents.

About the role:

We are hiring a Machine Learning Scientist to train, validate and ship the predictive models that power our molecular design platform. You will build models that score chemical molecules for developability (ADMET), potency, synthesizability and 3D structure, working alongside chemists, biologists and platform engineers.

In your first year, success means two or three models in production use by project teams, each with documented benchmarks, calibrated uncertainty and a clear applicability domain.

What you will do:

Train and maintain ML models for ADMET and developability endpoints such as solubility, permeability, metabolic stability, toxicity and aggregation risk.
Build potency and binding models (QSAR, ligand- and structure-based) to rank and prioritize molecules against targets.
Develop synthesizability models: synthetic accessibility scoring, reaction-outcome prediction and retrosynthesis-informed filters.
Apply and fine-tune structure-aware models (GNNs, equivariant networks, protein-ligand structure and docking-informed ML).
Curate and clean assay data, define scaffold- or time-split benchmarks, and quantify uncertainty and applicability domain.
Package models for the platform with engineers: versioned, reproducible and monitored for drift.
Present results and limits of each model to chemists and project teams, and incorporate their feedback into retraining.

What you bring:

PhD in computational chemistry, cheminformatics, machine learning or a related field, or an MS plus equivalent industry experience (about 3-6 years of hands-on modeling).
Demonstrated experience training and validating ML models on chemical or molecular data, in industry or academia, with shipped or published results.
Direct experience with at least two of: ADMET/developability, potency/binding, synthesizability/retrosynthesis, protein or ligand structure.
Fluency with molecular representations (fingerprints, descriptors, graphs, 3D) and tools such as RDKit.
Strong Python and a deep learning framework (PyTorch preferred); experience with GNNs or transformers on molecules.
Rigorous evaluation habits: scaffold or temporal splits, baselines, noisy-label handling and uncertainty estimation.
Clear communication with chemists and biologists.

Nice to have:

Publications, open-source contributions or competition results in molecular ML.
Experience with generative design, active learning or Bayesian optimization loops.
Experience with large-scale training, MLOps and model serving.
Familiarity with docking, free-energy methods or protein structure prediction tools.
Experience working with biologics or non-small-molecule modalities.
