Raritan, New Jersey, United States of America, Spring House, Pennsylvania, United States of America, Titusville, New Jersey, United States of America

Job Description

Our expertise in Innovative Medicine is informed and inspired by patients, whose insights fuel our science-based advancements. Visionaries like you work on teams that save lives by developing the medicines of tomorrow.

Join us in developing treatments, finding cures, and pioneering the path from lab to life while championing patients every step of the way.

Learn more at https://www.jnj.com/innovative-medicine

About The Opportunity

Johnson & Johnson Innovative Medicine is seeking a Principal Agentic Workflow & AI Engineer
to help build the agentic layer of our Biologics Discovery data engine. This is an opportunity to be one of the early, senior experts shaping how agentic AI workflows automate secondary data processing, orchestrate analyses, and connect experimental outputs to models and decisions across the DMTL (design-make-test-learn) cycle. You will work at the intersection of scientific experimentation, data pipelines, AI systems, and lab automation.

This position will be located at one of our office locations in either Spring House, PA (preferred), Titusville, NJ, or Raritan, NJ. (No remote option.)

Why this role matters:
Getting biologics data to flow reliably through our systems is a critical, often underestimated challenge, and there is significant opportunity to automate secondary analysis. This role brings agentic AI and intelligent automation to compress cycle time, reduce manual intervention, and improve reproducibility - transforming today’s hands-on processes into scalable, connected, intelligent discovery workflows. It is a strategically visible Principal-level role, central to our next-generation discovery automation.

Why This Role Is Unique

This is a rare chance to architect how scientific and physical AI come together to steer design and execution in the lab - not just automating steps but building a next-generation discovery engine in a large pharma setting. As a Principal individual contributor, your work will be among the most visible and influential on the team and will directly accelerate how tomorrow's therapies are discovered.

Position Summary

As a Principal Agentic Workflow & AI Engineer, you will design and build agentic workflows and orchestration that own the scientific data analysis and secondary processing logic our team delivers. You will translate scientific priorities into automation and AI roadmaps, and build real-time pipelines connecting automation software, data stores, models, and compute.

You will partner across Discovery, Data Science, In Silico Discovery (ISD), our Enterprise Generative AI team, and our data-infrastructure and lab-automation teams to enable closed-loop feedback so that each experimental cycle improves downstream models and decisions - timed to lab-automation readiness as new automation infrastructure comes online. You will also set technical direction and mentor other team members.

Key Responsibilities

Agentic Orchestration & Integration

Design, configure, and continuously improve agentic workflows that automate secondary analysis for biologics discovery assays, replacing fragile manual and ad-hoc scripted steps.
Build or oversee real-time pipelines connecting automation software, data stores, models, and compute environments.
Partner with IT and platform teams to implement resilient APIs, observability, versioning, and workflow orchestration end-to-end.
Partner with our Enterprise Generative AI team to build on shared GenAI platforms, models, and agentic frameworks - extending them for biologics discovery rather than duplicating enterprise capabilities.
Partner with ontology and MLOps colleagues so automated workflows produce semantically consistent, reusable data and deploy reliably into production.

AI-Driven Scientific Learning

Design workflows optimized for AI-driven learning, not just throughput, enabling closed-loop feedback across the design-make-test-learn (DMTL) cycle.
Collaborate with discovery scientists, AI/ML scientists, and data engineers so experimental outputs improve downstream property models and decision-making.
Ensure data generated through agentic workflows is high-quality, traceable, interoperable, and AI-ready, with strong metadata, provenance, and lineage.
Identify opportunities to apply agentic AI to compress cycle time and improve reproducibility.

Technical Leadership

Set technical direction and standards for agentic workflows and mentor engineers and data scientists across the AI/ML space.
Evaluate and pilot emerging agentic AI methods, frameworks, and tools, guiding where the team invests.
Represent the team's agentic work in cross-functional technical forums, aligning approaches with partner teams and enterprise standards.

Qualifications

Required

Advanced degree (Ph.D. preferred) in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related computational field.
At least 3 years experience building scientific workflow orchestration, automation software, including experience in agentic workflows and technical leadership responsibilities.
Hands-on experience designing real-time or near-real-time data pipelines and integrating complex and heterogeneous scientific data and instrument outputs.
Experience applying agentic AI and modern LLM-based agents (or comparable intelligent-automation systems) to scientific or laboratory workflows.
Experience building on enterprise or shared GenAI platforms and retrieval-augmented approaches (e.g., RAG or GraphRAG) rather than standing up capabilities from scratch.
Ability to translate scientific objectives into practical, scalable technical solutions and to set technical direction for others.
Strong communication and stakeholder management with comfort operating in ambiguity and representing work to leadership in matrixed organizations.

Preferred

Experience in drug discovery domains such as biologics, high-throughput experimentation, or imaging.
Exposure to lab automation, robotic systems, or cyber-physical systems for R&D.
Familiarity with MLOps/DevOps, workflow engines, and production-grade monitoring/observability.
Understanding of FAIR data, ontologies, semantic models, lineage/provenance, and AI-ready data standards.

This position will be located at one of our office locations in either Spring House, PA (preferred), Titusville, NJ, or Raritan, NJ. (No remote option.)

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, national origin, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by federal, state or local law. added.title: Agentic AI Security Engineer
added.description:
Company Description

About AbbVie

AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at www.abbvie.com. Follow @abbvie on LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram, X and YouTube.

Job Description

We are building a team that develops AI agents to solve real security problems -- detection, triage, response, risk assessment, and policy enforcement. This is a hands-on engineering role. You will design, build, test, and ship agentic AI systems that operate within our security stack.

You will work alongside senior engineers and researchers who are pushing the boundaries of what autonomous systems can do in cybersecurity. You will contribute production code from day one while developing deep expertise in both AI/ML and security operations.

Responsibilities:

Build and deploy AI agents that automate security workflows -- threat detection, alert triage, incident response, risk assessment, and compliance monitoring
Integrate large language models and other AI/ML capabilities with security tooling (SIEM, EDR, SOAR, cloud security platforms)
Develop and maintain agent orchestration pipelines, including prompt engineering, tool integration, and evaluation frameworks
Write Python (primarily) to build, test, and iterate on agent systems
Instrument agents with logging, monitoring, and metrics to measure effectiveness against security operations KPIs
Participate in adversarial testing of agent systems -- identify failure modes, edge cases, and security vulnerabilities in agent behavior
Collaborate with senior ICs to translate research concepts into production-ready systems
Contribute to agentic AI security policy, standards, and technical guidance -- informed by what you learn building and running these systems
Help shape best practices for safe and effective use of AI agents in security operations
Contribute to security position papers on emerging technologies -- high-level strategic documents that frame organizational thinking and drive downstream policy and technical guidance
Contribute to the AI Cybersecurity Maturity program across domains including application security, training, AI controls and infrastructure, AI discovery and inventory, operations and incident response, and policy and procedure development

Qualifications

Required:

Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or related field with 7 years’ experience; or Master’s Degree with 6 years’ experience; or PhD with 2 years’ experience.
Experience in cybersecurity, software engineering, or a closely related field
Strong Python skills - you can build, debug, and ship production systems
Hands-on experience with at least one area of security operation: threat intelligence, detection engineering, incident response, cloud security, or application security
Hands-on experience with agentic coding tools (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Aider, or similar) as part of your daily development workflow - we expect you to build with agents, not just build agents
Working knowledge of LLMs and AI/ML concepts -- you have built something with them, not just read about them
Experience integrating APIs and building data pipelines
Familiarity with security tooling (SIEM, EDR, vulnerability scanners, cloud security tools)
Experience building AI agents or automation systems - you have shipped something, not just experimented
Ability to work independently on well-scoped problems and collaboratively on ambiguous ones

Preferred:

Familiarity with agent orchestration frameworks and concepts (LangChain, AutoGen, custom frameworks)
Experience with cloud platforms (Azure, AWS, GCP) and their AI/ML services
Background in threat intelligence, detection engineering, or security automation (SOAR, playbooks)
Exposure to adversarial testing or red teaming of AI systems
Interest in or experience contributing to security policy, standards, or technical guidance
Master’s in computer science, Cybersecurity, or related field

added.title: Forward Deployed Engineer
added.description:
About Savvy Wealth

Wealth management is a $545 billion industry that still runs on manual work. 75% of advisors offer no digital communication beyond email, and most still build financial plans by hand in Excel. Savvy is reinventing what it looks like to be a financial advisor. Founder Ritik Malhotra saw the fragmentation firsthand after seeking out his own advisor, and started Savvy to give independent advisors a modern, AI-native home.

Savvy is a registered investment advisor (RIA), and we partner with experienced financial advisors who want to grow without running the back office themselves. Advisors bring their book and join Savvy, running under their own brand (or ours), and Savvy earns a percentage of the assets they manage. In return, they get a true business-in-a-box: a proprietary tech platform and client portal, an in-house marketing team that helps them grow, a world-class investment management team, and a dedicated client services team that runs day-to-day operations and support. Advisors at Savvy service up to 50% more households and save 19 hours a week.

AI runs through everything we do. On the product side, Savvy Intelligence (released April 2026) is the only AI built for wealth managers that can see a client's complete financial picture. Internally, everyone at Savvy uses Claude and is encouraged to experiment with it, backed by a dedicated AI enablement team and a RevOps org building agents in-house.

What makes the role distinctive is that the data that matters lives inside partners' own systems, so you make it usable, securely, and turn each deployment into reusable tooling that makes the next partner faster.

What would your day-to-day look like

Work on site with partner teams to connect to their systems, including on-premise and legacy platforms, and build secure, reliable data feeds.
Map messy, inconsistent commercial data from many sources into one clean model.
Build and run pipelines for large historical and near-real-time datasets, with monitoring and data quality checks.
Meet partners' security, privacy and IT review requirements, taking only the data the product needs.
Design, train and evaluate production ML models for a high-volume commercial use case, choosing the right approach and being clear about the trade-offs.
Build the evaluation and measurement that show whether the models are good enough, and where they aren't.
Build low-latency, high-throughput services that serve the models in production.
Design how the system decides what to answer and how, and how it improves from real usage.
Own reliability, cost and performance once the system is live.
Partner directly with technology and business teams, from first conversations to go-live.
Collaborate with Research and Product, feeding back what you learn in the field.
Turn each deployment into reusable tooling so the next partner goes faster.

An ideal candidate has

5+ years building and shipping production ML systems end to end, covering data, modelling, serving and monitoring, which you will apply to a high-volume commercial use case from day one.
Strong data engineering experience, having built and kept running pipelines over large, messy datasets, which you will use to turn partner data into one clean model.
Experience integrating with systems you don't control, such as enterprise, on-premise or legacy platforms, and working through a customer's security and IT review, so you can get partner data flowing securely.
Experience building and running services that handle thousands of requests per second at sub-second response times, which you will use to serve models in production.

added.title: Staff Forward Deployed Engineer
added.description:
Let's face it, a company whose mission is human transformation better have some fresh thinking about the employer/employee relationship.

We do. We can't cram it all in here, but you'll start noticing it from the first interview.

Even our candidate experience is different. And when you get an offer from us (and accept it), you get way more than a paycheck. You get a personal BetterUp Coach, a development plan, a trained and coached manager, the most amazing team you've ever met (yes, each with their own personal BetterUp Coach), and most importantly, work that matters.

This makes for a remarkably focused and fulfilling work experience. Frankly, it's not for everyone. But for people with fire in their belly, it's a game-changing, career-defining, soul-lifting move.

Join us and we promise you the most intense and fulfilling years of your career, doing life-changing work in a fun, inventive, soulful culture.

If that sounds exciting—and the job description below feels like a fit—we really should start talking.

We are a hybrid company with a focus on in-person collaboration when necessary. Employees are expected to be available to work from one of our office hubs at least two days per week, or eight days per month. Our US hub locations include: Austin, TX; New York City, NY; San Francisco, CA; and the Washington, DC metro area. If this is a role based in Europe, our Europe hub locations are London, UK and Amsterdam, NL. Please ensure you can realistically commit to this structure before applying.

The Opportunity

AI is changing how every person in the world works. It's a new Industrial Revolution, and almost all of the attention is on the technology. Far less is going to the people who have to change how they work to use it.

We think helping people through that change is one of the most important problems in the world right now. Even the most technically advanced companies are struggling to get their workforces productive with AI, and our research shows much of the gap comes down to mindset and behavior, which can be coached. Coaching used to be something a company could afford only for its top leaders. With AI and human coaches working together, we can reach everyone, and the most iconic companies in the world are asking us to build that with them.

Our largest customers no longer decide on the demo. They decide on what happens after: whether their HR systems connect, whether provisioning works, whether coaching shows up inside the tools their people already have open, whether our AI behaves the way their risk team needs it to. Forward Deployment is the function that owns that work.

This role sets the technical architecture for Forward Deployment. Our largest customers are asking for the same few things in different words: the coach inside their own assistant, their data in their own lake, an AI deployment their governance committee will sign. Today we solve each of those one account at a time. You decide what the shared pattern is, build the first version on the hardest account, and make it what every squad uses and what the core platform eventually absorbs.

The accounts are specific. One customer wants our coach answering inside the agent platform it is rolling out to its whole workforce. Another is building its own experience layer on top of ours and needs an architecture where each experience is a declarative object instead of a custom build. A third signed, and then its AI governance committee asked how its data is hosted, whether it trains a model, and what happens under a legal hold.

You'll do this as a hands-on engineer, with squads of engineers and PMs around you, and you'll be the engineer we put in front of a customer's CTO, chief architect, or CISO when the technical answer decides the deal.

What You Own

Set the architecture on the hardest accounts in the book. You walk into a customer whose environment we don't know yet and leave with a design their architects accept, our engineers can build, and core engineering can live with.
Decide whether we build, configure, or refuse. Some asks are a week of configuration, some are a real build, and some would fork the product. You make that call early, in writing, and you defend it to the customer and to our own leadership.
Own the pattern for putting the coach inside a customer's front door. That means agent-to-agent integration on standard protocols like MCP and A2A, into Copilot, Teams, and customers' own agent platforms, designed once so the fifth customer is configuration.
Write the engineering standards for Forward Deployment. The security bar for customer-facing builds, sandbox and data isolation, customer-data handling, and what "ready to graduate" means. Our code touches HR systems and member data at customers who run us through security review, and the standards are yours to write and hold.
Own the seam with core engineering. Every custom build ends one of three ways: it graduates into the platform with core engineering's acceptance, it converts to paid work, or we kill it. You make the technical case at the monthly graduation board, and you design builds so the ones worth keeping can be accepted cleanly.
Build the shared deployment infrastructure. A real customer sandbox, the tooling that turns a customer's own material into a working context library, and the evaluation harness that tells us whether a configured coach behaves the way that customer needs. Each new account should start from what the last one built.
Carry the technical relationship where the decision sits. You'll work with a customer's CTO, CISO, and enterprise architects, and you'll write the answers on data hosting, model training, and legal holds that their governance committee asks for.
Keep building. You write code on the hardest problems yourself, and the first version of every shared pattern is yours.
Raise the bar for every Forward Deployed engineer. You won't manage people. The way you design, review, and document becomes how the other squads work.

What You'll Bring

7+ years building and shipping production software, including several years as the technical owner of systems deployed inside large enterprises.
A record of leading the technical side of customer deployments where the contract value ran into seven or eight figures.
Architecture depth across identity, data, and integration: single sign-on and provisioning, HRIS, data pipelines, and multi-tenant isolation. You've designed for a customer's security review and passed it.
Production experience with LLM and agent systems: tool use, retrieval and context, guardrails, and evaluation. You've been accountable for how an AI system behaved in front of real users.
Credibility with senior technical audiences on both sides of the table. You've briefed a customer's CTO or CISO and your own engineering leadership, and you've delivered bad news to both without losing the room.
A record of turning one-off customer work into platform capability, and of killing the work that didn't deserve it.
Experience with agent protocols (MCP, A2A) or building inside Microsoft Teams, Copilot, or Slack is a plus.
Domain expertise in organizational transformation, human transformation, or talent intelligence is a plus.

Skills & Competencies

Relentless agency. When something isn't working, you own it and fix it instead of naming the team that should have. Humility about what you don't know, and relentlessness about figuring it out anyway.
Architectural judgment under ambiguity. You pick the simplest design that survives the customer's constraints, and you can say what would make you change it.
The discipline to say no. A happy customer asking for one more thing is the hardest no in this job, and so is telling your own leadership that an ask would fork the product. You can do both without damaging the relationship.
Judgment about what generalizes. You can tell a custom build worth paving into the platform from one customer's snowflake, and you'll argue for the distinction in front of core engineering.
Executive technical communication. You can write the architecture note a CISO's team will read, and explain the same decision to a Chief People Officer in two minutes.
AI-native fluency. Building with agents is your default operating method, and you set the practices the rest of the team builds with.
Comfort deciding on incomplete information. You listen, synthesize, decide, and move. When you're wrong you correct fast and say so. You don't stall waiting for consensus.

Preferred Backgrounds

Senior forward deployed engineers and deployment leads from companies that run this model, who have owned the architecture across several accounts.
Staff and principal engineers or architects from enterprise platforms in identity, HR technology, or data, who know how large customers' systems behave once they're deployed.
Founders, CTOs, and founding engineers who sold into large enterprises and carried the security review themselves.
Applied AI leads who have put agent or LLM systems into production at large companies and answered for how they behaved.

Why This Role

Helping people adapt while AI changes how work gets done is one of the most important problems in the world right now. You'll work on it across entire workforces at many of the world's largest employers, a bigger scale than any one company's internal team gets.
You set the architecture for a function our executive team has named as its expansion lever, on the accounts where the technical answer decides the outcome.
Your work sits on the critical path of decisions worth millions of dollars, and you'll know within a quarter whether it moved them.
You'll build for some of the largest companies in the world, in their environment, with their engineers and architects. Nobody stands between you and the customer. If that's not appealing, this isn't the right role.
The custom work has somewhere to go. A monthly graduation board with core engineering decides what becomes a platform capability, and you're the one making the technical case.
The problems are current. Agent-to-agent integration, enterprise AI governance, and evaluating how a coach behaves across tens of thousands of people are open problems, and you'll work on them with customers who need answers this quarter.
Forward Deployment is a young function with unwritten rules. The person in this seat writes the technical ones.

AI at BetterUp

Our team thrives at the intersection of human expertise and AI capability. As an AI-forward company, adaptation and continuous learning are part of our daily work. We're looking for teammates who are excited to evolve alongside technology – people who experiment boldly, share their discoveries openly, and help define best practices for AI-augmented work. These professionals thoughtfully integrate AI into their work to deliver exceptional results while maintaining the human judgment and creativity that drives real innovation.

Benefits

At BetterUp, we are committed to living out our mission every day and that starts with providing benefits that allow our employees to care for themselves, support their families, and give back to their community.

Access to BetterUp coaching; one for you and one for a friend or family member
A competitive compensation plan with opportunity for advancement
Medical, dental, and vision insurance
Flexible paid time off
Per year:
All federal/statutory holidays observed
4 BetterUp Inner Workdays (https://www.betterup.co/inner-work)
5 Volunteer Days to give back
Company wide Summer & Winter breaks

Year-round charitable contribution of your choice on behalf of BetterUp
401(k) self contribution

We are dedicated to building diverse teams that fuel an authentic workplace and sense of belonging for each and every employee. We know applying for a job can be intimidating, please don’t hesitate to reach out — we encourage everyone interested in joining us to apply.

540 is seeking a Forward Deployed Engineer to support a high-impact Department of War (DoW) initiative focused on testing and evaluating advanced SI capabilities before they reach mission-critical environments. The program is building a secure, repeatable environment to evaluate agentic systems and language models across the DoW.

In this role, you will build, deploy, and operate a test and evaluation (T&E) harness inside a government-hosted environment. This harness will route evaluation traffic to models through a controlled gateway, orchestrate benchmark test runs, and produce auditable, verifiable results that government decision-makers can trust.

You will own the software from code to production and work directly with government and industry testers to evaluate large language models, distilled small language models, and multi-agent workflows. Ultimately, you will serve as the core technical partner who turns testing needs into working evaluations, delivering a robust reference implementation that the government will own and operate over the long term.

Location
: Primarily remote (DC metro area preferred), with occasional onsite meetings as needed

Citizenship & Clearance Requirement
: per client requirements, candidates must be U.S. Citizens with an active DoW Secret (or higher) clearance

Education Requirement:
Bachelor's Degree

540 Internal Thrive Level:
Forward Deployed Engineer III

WHY 540?

540 is a forward-thinking company that the government turns to in order to #getshitdone. We don't just talk about innovation – we deliver it. We break down barriers, build impactful technology, and solve mission-critical problems.

HOW YOU'LL DRIVE IMPACT

Build, extend, and manage the T&E harness in a Microsoft Azure Government environment at Impact Level 5 (IL5) while meeting strict privacy and regulatory requirements
Onboard new models, benchmarks, and datasets to support test campaigns for agentic systems, LLMs, and small language model (SLM) distillation
Design and deploy secure, containerized microservices and AI-enabled systems using automated CI/CD pipelines, leveraging GenAI tools to accelerate your own development workflow

added.title: Senior/Principal Forward Deployed Engineer, AI Products
added.description:
Your work days are brighter here.

We’re obsessed with making hard work pay off, for our people, our customers, and the world around us. As a Fortune 500 company and a leading AI platform for managing people, money, and agents, we’re shaping the future of work so teams can reach their potential and focus on what matters most. The minute you join, you’ll feel it. Not just in the products we build, but in how we show up for each other. Our culture is rooted in integrity, empathy, and shared enthusiasm. We’re in this together, tackling big challenges with bold ideas and genuine care. We look for curious minds and courageous collaborators who bring sun-drenched optimism and drive. Whether you're building smarter solutions, supporting customers, or creating a space where everyone belongs, you’ll do meaningful work with Workmates who’ve got your back. In return, we’ll give you the trust to take risks, the tools to grow, the skills to develop and the support of a company invested in you for the long haul. So, if you want to inspire a brighter work day for everyone, including yourself, you’ve found a match in Workday, and we hope to be a match for you too.

About The Team

You'll join the AI Products team, where we build Workday's AI agents from the ground up. Our mission is to bring these agents to life inside real customer environments — testing them against real data, real workflows, and real use cases.

We're early in the agent lifecycle, which means the work here is hands-on, fast-moving, and genuinely entrepreneurial: you'll often help write the playbook for how Workday deploys a new agent, rather than follow one that already exists. If you want to be close to the product at the exact moment it's taking shape, and to see your fieldwork directly change the product, this is the team to build inside.

About The Role

As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you'll work directly with some of Workday's most important early customers to deploy, configure, and improve our AI products and agents. You'll work alongside our product and engineering teams as an extension of our internal product managers, playing a central role in agent Early Access (EA) programs and running the customer deployments inside them.

Your mission is to make the product better by putting it to work in a live customer environment. A successful deployment is both a win for the customer and proof that the product is improving, so making early customers successful matters just as much as hardening the agent itself. You'll often be the first person at Workday to run a deployment of a given agent, so good judgment, clear communication, ownership, and organization will matter as much as technical curiosity.

Every deployment will surface something the product wasn't built for yet, so creative problem-solving and a "yes, and" mindset are core to this role: instead of telling a customer that something isn't possible, you'll find a way to solve their use case with what exists today, bring them along on what's coming next, and turn the gap into clear feedback for product and engineering.

In this role, you will:

Lead customer discovery to understand each customer's goals and what success looks like for them
Act as the day-to-day lead for design partners and EA customers: setting and resetting expectations, working with senior leaders across HR, Finance, and IT, and repairing relationships when a deployment hits a rough patch
Run EA deployments end to end: implement, configure, debug, and improve the solution through rapid iteration with direct customer feedback
Interpret customer tenant data, configuration, and unique workflows, and how the agent performs against them
Triage every issue quickly, sorting bugs from configuration issues, product gaps, and change-management needs, prioritize them, and route each to the right owner with the right urgency
Keep customers and internal teams updated on status, risks, and next steps
Turn customer feedback into clear problem statements, reproduction details, and evidence that product and engineering can act on to make the agent more accurate and reliable
Help define, measure, and assess the pre-GA stage gates and graduation scorecard for your product
Build playbooks, configuration patterns, and known-issue guides, and hand them off to the teams that scale deployments and build documentation
Partner closely with your product's program manager and the Workday Services lead on each customer project
Stay engaged through early GA until your product meets its graduation criteria, and remain a point of contact for major customers and future releases afterward

About You

Basic Qualifications - P4 (Senior)

7+ years of experience in product management, consulting, solutions engineering, implementation, or customer support within complex enterprise environments
Willingness and ability to travel up to 20% to customer sites as needed
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.

Basic Qualifications - P5 (Principal)

10+ years of experience in technical product management, solution architecture, forward deployed engineering, enterprise implementation, or principal-level consulting within complex enterprise SaaS ecosystems
Experience driving complex AI/ML, automation, or enterprise software deployments at scale with Fortune 500 executive stakeholders
Willingness and ability to travel up to 20% to customer sites as needed
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.

Other Qualifications

A demonstrated history of entrepreneurial ownership: you've built something from scratch, worked without a playbook, or driven an initiative end to end in an ambiguous environment, and you're energized by figuring out the right path when one doesn't already exist
Experience managing strategic customer relationships with senior leaders in key accounts — setting and resetting expectations, navigating organizational change, and rebuilding trust when a project hits a rough patch
Working knowledge of Workday, including business processes, security and permissions, tenant configuration, integrations, and how customers implement and govern Workday, so you can read a customer's tenant and understand how the agent will behave inside it

Each candidate’s compensation offer will be based on multiple factors including, but not limited to, geography, experience, skills, job duties, and business need, among other things. Our Approach to Flexible Work

With Flex Work, we’re combining the best of both worlds: in-person time and remote. Our approach enables our teams to deepen connections, maintain a strong community, and do their best work. We know that flexibility can take shape in many ways, so rather than a number of required days in-office each week, we simply spend at least half (50%) of our time each quarter in the office or in the field
with our customers, prospects, and partners (depending on role). This means you'll have the freedom to create a flexible schedule that caters to your business, team, and personal needs, while being intentional to make the most of time spent together. Those in our remote "home office" roles also have the opportunity to come together in our offices for important moments that matter.

added.title: Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) Consultant
added.description:
FDE & Agentic AI Architect Consultant

Seeking Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) Consultants with expertise in Agentic AI Architecture, Business Discovery, Solutioning, and Technical Leadership. The role is designed for someone who can engage directly with enterprise customers, identify business opportunities, architect AI solutions, and lead implementation through production deployment.

Ideal Consultant for this Role
: This position is a hybrid of an AI Solution Architect + Forward Deployed Engineer + Business Consultant, rather than a conventional AI Architect. The key differentiator should be the ability to discover business problems, articulate solutions to executives, and lead hands-on implementation.

Job Role
: FDE (Forward Deployed Engineering) Consultant & Agentic AI Architect
Role Type
: Client-facing, hands-on technical leadership
Required Experience
: 12–18 years overall experience, with strong hands-on AI engineering and architecture experience

Position Overview

We are looking for a seasoned FDE/Agentic AI Architect who combines strong business consulting, solution architecture, and hands-on engineering to design and deliver enterprise-grade Agentic AI solutions.
The ideal candidate will work closely with business stakeholders, technology leaders, and engineering teams to understand complex business challenges, identify AI-driven transformation opportunities, and translate business requirements into scalable Agentic AI architectures and solutions.
This role requires a blend of business acumen, technical depth, architectural thinking, communication, and leadership skills. The candidate will own the journey from business discovery and solution conceptualization through architecture, prototyping, implementation, and production deployment.

Key Responsibilities
A. Business Discovery & Solutioning
Lead business discovery workshops with enterprise customers and senior stakeholders.
Understand business processes, identify pain points, and uncover opportunities for AI-led automation and transformation.
Translate business challenges into AI use cases, solution concepts, and implementation roadmaps.
Evaluate business feasibility, technical complexity, ROI, and expected business outcomes.
Develop solution proposals, architecture presentations, proofs-of-concept, and technical demonstrations.
Collaborate with sales, consulting, and delivery teams to shape AI opportunities and drive solution adoption.

B. Agentic AI Architecture & Engineering
Design and architect enterprise-scale Agentic AI solutions involving autonomous and collaborative AI agents.
Define multi-agent architectures, orchestration patterns, agent workflows, and decision-making frameworks.
Architect solutions using LLMs, RAG, vector databases, knowledge graphs, and enterprise data sources.
Design agent memory, context management, tool integration, and human-in-the-loop capabilities.
Establish guardrails, security, governance, observability, and responsible AI practices.
Evaluate and select appropriate LLMs, AI frameworks, and infrastructure based on business requirements.
Drive development of scalable, secure, reliable, and production-ready AI applications.

C. Technical Leadership & Delivery
Provide technical direction and architectural leadership to cross-functional engineering teams.
Lead solution prototyping, technical validation, and production implementation.
Work closely with developers, data engineers, cloud architects, and platform teams.
Establish engineering standards, reusable architecture patterns, and best practices.
Review solution designs and ensure performance, scalability, security, and maintainability.
Drive technical problem-solving and resolve complex architectural challenges.

D. Communication & Stakeholder Management
Act as a trusted technical advisor to business executives, technology leaders, and customers.
Communicate complex AI concepts and architectural decisions in business-friendly language.
Present solution approaches, technical roadmaps, and business value propositions.
Facilitate discussions between business stakeholders and engineering teams.
Demonstrate strong ownership, collaboration, influencing, and leadership capabilities.

Required Technical Skills and Experience

Strong understanding of Generative AI, LLMs, and Agentic AI architectures.
Hands-on experience with multi-agent frameworks such as LangGraph, LangChain, CrewAI, AutoGen, or equivalent.
Experience designing RAG architectures, semantic search, embeddings, and vector databases.
Strong Python programming and API integration experience.
Experience with LLM orchestration, prompt engineering, tool/function calling, and context management.
Hands-on MCP (Model Context Protocol) and enterprise tool integration.
Experience with cloud AI platforms such as AWS Bedrock, Azure AI Foundry, or Google Vertex AI.
Understanding of AI evaluation, tracing, observability, and performance optimization.
Experience with enterprise security, data privacy, AI governance, and responsible AI principles.
Hands-on with Docker, Kubernetes, CI/CD, and cloud-native application architectures.

Leadership & Consulting Competencies
Strong business consulting and problem-solving mindset.
Excellent customer-facing communication and presentation skills.
Ability to lead discovery workshops and architecture discussions.
Ability to translate ambiguous business problems into actionable technical solutions.
Strong executive stakeholder management and influencing skills.
Experience mentoring and leading engineering teams.
Ability to operate independently in fast-paced, customer-facing environments.
Strong ownership and accountability from solution conceptualization through delivery.

Experience & Qualifications
12–18 years of overall experience in software engineering, enterprise architecture, solution consulting, or technology leadership.
At least 3–5 years of hands-on experience in Generative AI / LLM-based solution development and architecture.
Demonstrated experience designing and delivering enterprise AI solutions.
Experience in customer-facing architecture, consulting, and solution engineering roles.
Proven track record of leading complex technology initiatives from discovery through implementation.

Preferred Qualifications:
Experience in Forward Deployed Engineering or AI solution consulting roles.
Experience building production-grade multi-agent AI systems.
Experience in enterprise digital transformation and intelligent automation.
Exposure to industry-specific AI solutions across healthcare, financial services, manufacturing, or other enterprise domains.
Experience defining AI adoption strategies and enterprise AI roadmaps.

Success Criteria:
The successful candidate will be expected to:
Identify and qualify high-value business opportunities for Agentic AI.
Translate business requirements into differentiated AI solution architectures.
Lead customer engagements, solution demonstrations, and technical discussions.
Build functional prototypes and guide engineering teams toward production implementation.
Accelerate enterprise adoption of Agentic AI solutions.
Deliver measurable business outcomes through AI-driven innovation.

added.title: Forward Deployed Engineer
added.description:
About Northwood:

Northwood is a modern space infrastructure company bringing the benefits of space to the masses through advanced communications technology. We are building a global network of phased array and parabolic ground stations that enable real-time, reliable communication for satellite missions such as national security, global connectivity, and disaster response. With a vertically integrated approach, Northwood designs, builds, and rapidly deploys scalable systems that power the next generation of space missions. If you like solving complex challenges and seeing your work deployed around the world with real impact, Northwood is the place to do it.

Role:

The Forward Deployed Engineer will help customers adopt and succeed on Northwood's ground station network. You'll work with satellite operators to understand their missions, shape requirements, and guide them from first conversation through deployment and beyond. You'll partner closely with Business Development, Engineering, and Program Management throughout.

This role suits a technically credible operator who can build trust with satellite customers, spot opportunities, and turn mission needs into clear priorities for our internal teams.

Responsibilities:

Make customer missions succeed on Northwood's network.
Serve as the primary technical contact for customers during capture, evaluation, onboarding, and post-deployment.
Get hands-on with implementation and integration — working directly alongside customers and Engineering to bring up, troubleshoot, and validate their operations on the network.
Ship code, debug integrations, and validate operations alongside customers and Engineering
Support Business Development on qualification, proposals, and expansion.
Lead technical discovery, exchanges, demos, and readiness reviews alongside Program Management.
Learn each customer's mission, workflows, constraints, decision criteria, and success metrics in depth.
Translate customer needs into clear priorities for Engineering, Product, and BD.
Surface friction points, adoption blockers, and recurring needs that should shape the product and network.
Coordinate onboarding and deployment readiness — clarifying requirements, flagging risks, and aligning internal teams around customer objectives.
Build reusable discovery frameworks and customer-facing materials that help Northwood scale capture and customer success.

Basic Qualifications:

7+ years in customer-facing technical roles: solutions or systems engineering, mission operations, technical business development, capture engineering, solutions architecture, or TAM.
Bachelor's in EE, CE, CS, Aerospace, or related field — or equivalent experience with mission systems, ground systems, networking, cloud, or satellite operations.
Track record taking complex customer engagements from discovery through deployment or expansion.
Proven ability to build trust with technical customers and turn ambiguous mission needs into concrete priorities.
Comfortable working in ambiguous environments spanning hardware, software, networking, and business objectives.
Strong communicator — able to lead technical conversations, write clear customer materials, and brief internal stakeholders.
Effective across BD, Engineering, Product, Program Management, and customer teams.
Willing to travel up to 30%.

Preferred Qualifications:

Background in satellite communications, RF, space operations, ground stations, or telecom infrastructure.
Experience with proposals, technical evaluations, demos, pilots, or proof-of-concept work.
Experience managing technical relationships in mission-critical environments.
Familiarity with APIs, networking protocols, telemetry, scheduling systems, cloud infrastructure, or mission assurance.
Ability to obtain or hold TS/SCI clearance.

Additional Requirements:

This position requires successfully obtaining and maintaining a Top Secret Security Clearance as a condition of employment. While the clearance may not be immediately necessary upon hire, we encourage you to initiate the application process promptly upon accepting this offer. Your ability to secure the necessary clearance is essential for fulfilling key responsibilities of the role. Should you be unable to obtain it, Northwood Space reserves the right to modify or terminate your employment to align with optional needs.
Must be willing to work extended hours and weekends as needed
This role requires being on-site 5 days per week

Additional Information:

To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.

Northwood Space is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with Northwood Space is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.

If you need a reasonable accommodation as part of your application for employment or interviews with us, please let us know at accommodations@northwoodspace.io

added.title: Applied AI Architect, Public Sector (Federal Civilan)
added.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About The Role

As an Applied AI team member at Anthropic, you will be a Pre-Sales architect focused on becoming a trusted technical advisor helping federal civilian government agencies understand the value of Claude and paint the vision on how they can successfully integrate and deploy Claude into their technology stack. You'll combine your deep technical expertise with customer-facing skills to architect innovative LLM solutions that address complex mission challenges while maintaining our high standards for safety and reliability.

Working closely with our Sales, Product, and Engineering teams, you'll guide customers from initial technical discovery through successful deployment. You'll leverage your expertise to help customers understand Claude's capabilities, develop evals, and design scalable architectures that maximize the value of our AI systems.

added.title: Principal Content Solutions Architect, Streaming Audio
added.description:
Xperi invents, develops and delivers technologies that create extraordinary experiences at home and on the go for millions of people around the world. Powering billions of consumer electronics, connected cars and digital content titles, we make entertainment more immersive, driving more intelligent and every interaction seamlessly personalized through our renowned consumer brands: DTS®, HD Radio™ and TiVo®.      Xperi (NYSE: XPER) is a publicly traded technology company headquartered in San Jose, CA with over 1,450 employees across North America, Europe and Asia. Come join a thriving team where you can play an integral role in shaping the future of entertainment technology.    The Principal Content Solutions Architect, Streaming Audio is the senior technical authority and advisor to content service providers (CSPs) integrating DTS premium audio, primarily DTS:X, into their streaming services. CSPs own their integration; this role guides them from discovery through launch by recommending end-to-end audio architectures, integration planning and troubleshooting approaches supporting each stage of DTS audio delivery: encoding, packaging, signaling and device playback. Based in Calabasas, California and reporting to the Director, Engineering Operations, the role connects CSPs with Xperi product management, content business development and audio technology teams to help resolve issues, recommend validation criteria, and turn partner needs into architectural guidance and product requirements. 

Essential Duties & Responsibilities 

Partner technical advisor: Primary technical contact and trusted architectural advisor for CSPs adopting DTS and DTS:X, from discovery and proof of concept through launch and post-launch support, owning follow-through on commitments made to CSPs. 

Audio integration requirements: Define DTS:X streaming format and packaging requirements and advise CSPs on encoding parameters, metadata, codec signaling (codec strings, MIME types, sample entries), fMP4 packaging, and HLS, MPEG-DASH and CMAF manifest signaling. 

Troubleshooting support: Guide CSPs through root-cause analysis of audio issues; request streams, logs, device details and reproduction steps; compare behavior against reference players; help isolate the likely fault; recommend fixes, track to closure and communicate status, root cause and known limitations candidly. 

Playback path guidance: Advise CSPs on playback architecture, including device capability detection, decoder selection, decode vs. passthrough vs. transcode, audio track selection and fallback in multi-codec ladders. 

Codec switching and ad insertion: Advise on architecture and validation of audio behavior at codec transitions and SSAI/AVOD ad boundaries, including timestamp continuity, segment alignment and audio loss on switch; help diagnose issues found in CSP testing. 

Technical documentation: Author partner-facing integration guides, application notes, best practices, test procedures and architecture diagrams so CSPs can integrate independently. 

Requirements and roadmap input: Collect and prioritize CSP requirements and market feedback; present them to Product Management and Engineering. 

Cross-functional coordination: Liaison between content business development, CSPs and internal engineering, product, certification and commercial teams. Translate partner needs into clear requests for engineering-delivered validation assets, reference streams, test plans, tooling and certification support. Track dependencies; communicate risks, decisions and status transparently and set realistic expectations with CSPs on timelines and product capabilities.  

Education and/or Experience 

Required: 

Bachelor’s degree in computer science, electrical engineering, audio engineering or a related field, or equivalent experience 

10+ years in streaming media, audio/codec technology or media platform engineering, including significant customer-facing time (solutions architecture, solutions engineering, field applications, technical account management or partner integration) 

Hands-on experience with multichannel and immersive audio codecs in streaming (DTS:X, Dolby Atmos/E-AC-3 JOC, MPEG-H and others) 

Strong practical knowledge of OTT delivery (HLS, MPEG-DASH, CMAF, fragmented MP4/ISO BMFF, MPEG-TS) for live and on-demand streaming: manifests, segmentation, timestamps and adaptive bitrate switching 

Android TV/Google TV playback (AndroidX Media3/ExoPlayer, MediaCodec, AudioTrack, tunnel mode, direct passthrough); smart TV or browser (MSE) playback 

Experience architecting and supporting commercial launches with streaming services, content providers and/or platform operators  

Proven experience designing end-to-end streaming audio delivery architectures, from encoding and packaging through device playback 

Preferred: 

Working knowledge of downstream audio playback, including A/V sync and HDMI/eARC behavior with soundbars and AV receivers 

DRM and secure playback (Widevine, PlayReady, FairPlay) 

SSAI/AVOD workflows and cloud encoding and packaging (e.g., AWS Elemental MediaTailor, MediaConvert, MediaLive) 

C/C++ sufficient to read, build and debug codec SDK and player integration code on Linux, ARM and embedded platforms 

Technical Proficiencies 

Stream and packaging analysis: FFmpeg/ffprobe, Bento4, GPAC/MP4Box, Shaka Packager, MediaInfo, DASH-IF conformance tools, Apple HLS stream validation tools or equivalent 

Players and device diagnostics: AndroidX Media3/ExoPlayer, Shaka Player, dash.js, hls.js, GStreamer or equivalent; Android debugging (adb, logcat, dumpsys); log collection on smart TV and set-top platforms; network capture and browser developer tools for MSE playback 

Scripting and automation: Python and shell for stream inspection and diagnostic analysis; Git for version control 

Documentation and diagramming: Confluence, Microsoft Office (including PowerPoint for architecture presentations); architecture and signal-flow diagramming tools 

Partner collaboration: Jira or equivalent for tracking partner issues to closure; video conferencing and remote-session tools for live issue reproduction with CSPs 

AI tools: Generative AI assistants for drafting and summarization (e.g., Microsoft Copilot, Claude, ChatGPT); AI coding assistants for scripting and log analysis (e.g., GitHub Copilot) 

Other Skills & Abilities 

Presents architectures, technical work and recommendations to partners, customers and all levels of the company; leads external technical discussions and brings in other functions as needed 

Writes complex architecture and technical documents for internal, partner and customer audiences at the right level of detail 

Turns ambiguous partner questions into testable hypotheses, acceptance criteria, integration options and actionable recommendations 

Weighs technical and business tradeoffs; sets priorities and judges risk and schedule across concurrent partner engagements 

Influences across organizational boundaries without direct authority; builds networks beyond own area of expertise 

Advises partners consultatively and works with product management, content business development to scope CSP opportunities and translate them into technical plans 

Customer-oriented and accountable: owns commitments to partners, follows through, and communicates candidly when plans or capabilities change 

Acts with integrity. Represents Xperi and its technology honestly and builds partner trust through consistency and reliability. 

Home office: Calabasas, California (hybrid, 3 days per week in office) 

Authorized to work in the United States 

Up to 25% global travel for customer visits and industry events

We are dedicated to creating a workplace where all employees have a voice and sense of belonging, feel safe and valued, and are acknowledged for how their unique differences contribute to organizational culture and business outcomes.   Our employees and their families are important to us, and our comprehensive pay, stock and benefits programs reflect that. Xperi supports personal well-being, builds financial security and enables employees to share in our collective success.   Rewards include:    Competitive compensation (salary, equity and bonuses) and comprehensive benefits designed to foster work-life balance, care for your health, protect your finances and help you save and invest for the future.

Senior Solution Architect, AI & Platform

United States

As a Senior Solution Architect, AI & Platform, you will serve as a technical authority for complex enterprise opportunities, owning architecture across telephony, networking, VDI, public cloud, APIs, and AI-powered solutions spanning self-service, agent assistance, journey management, and back-office automation.

You will partner with account teams, customers, Professional Services, Product Management, and Engineering to move strategic opportunities from technical discovery through validation and production pilots. This role offers direct visibility with CIO, CTO, and senior technical stakeholders and the opportunity to influence both customer architecture and Genesys product direction. You will also expand the capabilities of the broader Solution Consulting organization through reusable architecture patterns, technical enablement, and field insight.

At Genesys, collaboration means bringing deep expertise together to solve meaningful customer challenges. In this role, you will help enterprises apply modern AI and cloud technologies to improve customer and employee experiences while influencing how those capabilities scale across complex environments.

Lead technical discovery, architecture, whiteboarding, customized demonstrations, trial engagements, and value assessments that advance complex enterprise opportunities from evaluation to validated solution design

Architect production-ready AI solutions that combine LLMs, deterministic workflows, tools, orchestration, human handoffs, and fallback strategies to improve customer and employee experiences

Establish AI evaluation and observability frameworks that connect accuracy, retrieval quality, tool-call performance, containment, safety, drift, latency, and cost with customer and business outcomes

added.title: Forward Deployed AI Engineer, Travel Intelligence
added.description:
About The Role

Hopper powers travel for some of the world’s largest banks, airlines and travel companies, and our Research team builds travel-specialized models. As a Forward Deployed AI Engineer you take that work into a partner’s environment and make it theirs: building the evaluation with their team, preparing their data, training and evaluating the model, and putting it into production where it delivers measurable results. You work in a small forward-deployed team as the person who leads model training on site, across servicing, loyalty, commerce and more, and you are the bridge between our partners and Research.

What Would Your Day-to-day Look Like

Work with a partner’s data and business teams to turn their real tasks into a frozen, held-out benchmark across their priority use cases
Define what success means for each task, covering task completion, policy adherence, cost and response time, and build the automated graders with human spot checks
Establish baselines so results can be compared fairly
Prepare training data inside the partner’s environment through extraction, redaction, deduplication, labelling and train/test splits, using only the data the agreed tasks need
Run post-training in partnership with Research, applying modern fine-tuning methods to partner use cases
Run training on the partner’s cloud and GPUs, or in an environment they approve, under their security and access rules
Design experiments that show partners clearly what drives the results
Take models from evaluation into production based on evidence, then monitor quality, latency and cost once they are live
Use production results to keep improving the model
Present results, method and trade-offs to partner data and technology leaders, and defend them
Work closely with Research, feeding back what you learn in the field
Turn each deployment into reusable tooling so the next partner goes faster
Uphold strict data handling, privacy and security standards in every partner environment, and support partner model-risk, security and compliance reviews with clear documentation of data, training and evaluation

An ideal candidate has

Run the full post-training loop end to end themselves, from data preparation through fine-tuning an open-weight model, evaluation and serving, rather than only calling a vendor’s fine-tuning service
Working experience with supervised fine-tuning and at least one of preference optimization or reinforcement learning, including parameter-efficient methods such as LoRA
Strong Python and command of the standard training stack, for example PyTorch, Hugging Face and vLLM, with comfort running jobs on rented or customer GPUs
Built benchmarks and graders from messy real-world data and used them to show that one model beats another on quality, cost and latency
A habit of thinking in held-out sets, baselines and ablations, and can explain a result’s limits as clearly as its headline
At least two deployments embedded with an enterprise customer, working inside their systems, data controls and security reviews
Confidence presenting to and pushing back on senior customer stakeholders, including data and technology leaders
Strong data engineering skills across SQL, pipelines, PII handling and redaction
An understanding of the privacy, security and model-risk requirements of regulated customers such as banks and airlines
Willingness to travel and spend multi-week stretches on site with partners, plus a base in the Eastern or Central time zone with daily overlap across the partner and Research teams you work with
Bonus: forward-deployed, applied research or applied AI experience at an AI-native company that trains its own models for a domain
Bonus: multilingual training and evaluation, or experience with travel, airline or banking systems and data such as PSS, GDS, NDC, ticketing, loyalty and contact-centre data
Bonus: experience with agent systems and tool use, or working alongside a research team to turn their methods into results at a customer

Perks And Benefits Of Working With Us

Well-funded and proven startup with large ambitions, competitive salary and the upsides of pre-IPO equity packages
Unlimited PTO
Carrot Cash travel stipend
Access to co-working space on demand through FlexDesk AND Work-from-home stipend
Please ask us about our very generous parental leave, much above industry standards!
Entrepreneurial culture where pushing limits and taking risks is everyday business
Open communication with management and company leadership
Small, dynamic teams = massive impact
100% employer paid Medical, Dental and Vision coverage for employees
Access to Disability & Life insurance
Health Reimbursement Account (HRA)
DCA/ FSA and access to 401k plan

About Hopper

At Hopper, we’re building the leading travel technology platform in the world, and we’re doing it by solving real problems for real travelers globally. Our Hopper consumer booking platforms and HTS (Hopper Technology Solutions), our B2B business, work together to give travelers something the industry has never reliably offered: transparency, flexibility, and real savings on every trip. We combine massive amounts of data and AI with proprietary fintech products to make that happen, not just another booking engine, but a fundamentally better way to plan and experience travel for our customers and our partners. We are proof that better-for-the-customer and better-for-the-business can be one in the same

And we’re continuing to grow fast! The Hopper app has been downloaded over 120 million times, with 70% of our users being Gen Z and Millennials, next-generation travelers. Today, our biggest opportunity is powering travel fintech, commerce, and loyalty for some of the biggest brands in the industry. Our first HTS partnership with Capital One helped launch a dedicated travel portal for a major financial brand’s cardholders, and we’ve since expanded across some of the biggest names in travel and banking, including Air Canada, Uber, Royal Bank of Canada (RBC), and Nubank, powering everything from a single fintech integration to a full end-to-end travel loyalty portal.

That’s our trajectory: we started as a small, disruptive app within the travel space, and now we’re the engine under the hood powering how Travel Tech works.

What That Looks Like In Practice

Billions of dollars in travel and travel fintech move through Hopper and HTS every year.
Our fintech products, including Cancel for Any Reason and Disruption Assistance for Any Reason, post exceptionally strong customer satisfaction because the terms are clear and resolutions are instant, no questions asked.
Nearly 30% of app customers add a fintech product to their booking, and those customers are 1.6x more likely to book with us again.
HTS now drives more than 90% of the business, proof of how fast B2B has scaled.
Through HTS, any travel provider (airlines, hotels, banks, travel agencies) can plug the company’s fintech, commerce and AI solutions into their own channels, whether that’s a single integration or a full end-to-end travel portal.

Come take off with us!

added.description:
At Johnson & Johnson, we believe health is everything. Our strength in healthcare innovation empowers us to build a world where complex diseases are prevented, treated, and cured, where treatments are smarter and less invasive, and solutions are personal. Through our expertise in Innovative Medicine and MedTech, we are uniquely positioned to innovate across the full spectrum of healthcare solutions today to deliver the breakthroughs of tomorrow, and profoundly impact health for humanity. Learn more at jnj.com.

As guided by Our Credo, Johnson & Johnson is responsible to our employees who work with us throughout the world. We provide an inclusive work environment where each person is considered as an individual. At Johnson & Johnson, we respect the diversity and dignity of our employees and recognize their merit.

Job Function

Data Analytics & Computational Sciences

Job Sub Function

Data Engineering

Job Category

Scientific/Technology

All Job Posting Locations:

Raritan, New Jersey, United States of America, Spring House, Pennsylvania, United States of America, Titusville, New Jersey, United States of America

Job Description

Our expertise in Innovative Medicine is informed and inspired by patients, whose insights fuel our science-based advancements. Visionaries like you work on teams that save lives by developing the medicines of tomorrow.

Join us in developing treatments, finding cures, and pioneering the path from lab to life while championing patients every step of the way.

Learn more at https://www.jnj.com/innovative-medicine

About The Opportunity

Johnson & Johnson Innovative Medicine is seeking a Principal Agentic Workflow & AI Engineer
to help build the agentic layer of our Biologics Discovery data engine. This is an opportunity to be one of the early, senior experts shaping how agentic AI workflows automate secondary data processing, orchestrate analyses, and connect experimental outputs to models and decisions across the DMTL (design-make-test-learn) cycle. You will work at the intersection of scientific experimentation, data pipelines, AI systems, and lab automation.

This position will be located at one of our office locations in either Spring House, PA (preferred), Titusville, NJ, or Raritan, NJ. (No remote option.)

Why this role matters:
Getting biologics data to flow reliably through our systems is a critical, often underestimated challenge, and there is significant opportunity to automate secondary analysis. This role brings agentic AI and intelligent automation to compress cycle time, reduce manual intervention, and improve reproducibility - transforming today’s hands-on processes into scalable, connected, intelligent discovery workflows. It is a strategically visible Principal-level role, central to our next-generation discovery automation.

Why This Role Is Unique

This is a rare chance to architect how scientific and physical AI come together to steer design and execution in the lab - not just automating steps but building a next-generation discovery engine in a large pharma setting. As a Principal individual contributor, your work will be among the most visible and influential on the team and will directly accelerate how tomorrow's therapies are discovered.

Position Summary

As a Principal Agentic Workflow & AI Engineer, you will design and build agentic workflows and orchestration that own the scientific data analysis and secondary processing logic our team delivers. You will translate scientific priorities into automation and AI roadmaps, and build real-time pipelines connecting automation software, data stores, models, and compute.

You will partner across Discovery, Data Science, In Silico Discovery (ISD), our Enterprise Generative AI team, and our data-infrastructure and lab-automation teams to enable closed-loop feedback so that each experimental cycle improves downstream models and decisions - timed to lab-automation readiness as new automation infrastructure comes online. You will also set technical direction and mentor other team members.

Key Responsibilities

Agentic Orchestration & Integration

Design, configure, and continuously improve agentic workflows that automate secondary analysis for biologics discovery assays, replacing fragile manual and ad-hoc scripted steps.
Build or oversee real-time pipelines connecting automation software, data stores, models, and compute environments.
Partner with IT and platform teams to implement resilient APIs, observability, versioning, and workflow orchestration end-to-end.
Partner with our Enterprise Generative AI team to build on shared GenAI platforms, models, and agentic frameworks - extending them for biologics discovery rather than duplicating enterprise capabilities.
Partner with ontology and MLOps colleagues so automated workflows produce semantically consistent, reusable data and deploy reliably into production.

AI-Driven Scientific Learning

Design workflows optimized for AI-driven learning, not just throughput, enabling closed-loop feedback across the design-make-test-learn (DMTL) cycle.
Collaborate with discovery scientists, AI/ML scientists, and data engineers so experimental outputs improve downstream property models and decision-making.
Ensure data generated through agentic workflows is high-quality, traceable, interoperable, and AI-ready, with strong metadata, provenance, and lineage.
Identify opportunities to apply agentic AI to compress cycle time and improve reproducibility.

Technical Leadership

Set technical direction and standards for agentic workflows and mentor engineers and data scientists across the AI/ML space.
Evaluate and pilot emerging agentic AI methods, frameworks, and tools, guiding where the team invests.
Represent the team's agentic work in cross-functional technical forums, aligning approaches with partner teams and enterprise standards.
