added.title: Staff Forward Deployed Engineer
added.description:
Let's face it, a company whose mission is human transformation better have some fresh thinking about the employer/employee relationship.

We do. We can't cram it all in here, but you'll start noticing it from the first interview.

Even our candidate experience is different. And when you get an offer from us (and accept it), you get way more than a paycheck. You get a personal BetterUp Coach, a development plan, a trained and coached manager, the most amazing team you've ever met (yes, each with their own personal BetterUp Coach), and most importantly, work that matters.

This makes for a remarkably focused and fulfilling work experience. Frankly, it's not for everyone. But for people with fire in their belly, it's a game-changing, career-defining, soul-lifting move.

Join us and we promise you the most intense and fulfilling years of your career, doing life-changing work in a fun, inventive, soulful culture.

If that sounds exciting—and the job description below feels like a fit—we really should start talking.

We are a hybrid company with a focus on in-person collaboration when necessary. Employees are expected to be available to work from one of our office hubs at least two days per week, or eight days per month. Our US hub locations include: Austin, TX; New York City, NY; San Francisco, CA; and the Washington, DC metro area. If this is a role based in Europe, our Europe hub locations are London, UK and Amsterdam, NL. Please ensure you can realistically commit to this structure before applying.

The Opportunity

AI is changing how every person in the world works. It's a new Industrial Revolution, and almost all of the attention is on the technology. Far less is going to the people who have to change how they work to use it.

We think helping people through that change is one of the most important problems in the world right now. Even the most technically advanced companies are struggling to get their workforces productive with AI, and our research shows much of the gap comes down to mindset and behavior, which can be coached. Coaching used to be something a company could afford only for its top leaders. With AI and human coaches working together, we can reach everyone, and the most iconic companies in the world are asking us to build that with them.

Our largest customers no longer decide on the demo. They decide on what happens after: whether their HR systems connect, whether provisioning works, whether coaching shows up inside the tools their people already have open, whether our AI behaves the way their risk team needs it to. Forward Deployment is the function that owns that work.

This role sets the technical architecture for Forward Deployment. Our largest customers are asking for the same few things in different words: the coach inside their own assistant, their data in their own lake, an AI deployment their governance committee will sign. Today we solve each of those one account at a time. You decide what the shared pattern is, build the first version on the hardest account, and make it what every squad uses and what the core platform eventually absorbs.

The accounts are specific. One customer wants our coach answering inside the agent platform it is rolling out to its whole workforce. Another is building its own experience layer on top of ours and needs an architecture where each experience is a declarative object instead of a custom build. A third signed, and then its AI governance committee asked how its data is hosted, whether it trains a model, and what happens under a legal hold.

You'll do this as a hands-on engineer, with squads of engineers and PMs around you, and you'll be the engineer we put in front of a customer's CTO, chief architect, or CISO when the technical answer decides the deal.

What You Own

Set the architecture on the hardest accounts in the book. You walk into a customer whose environment we don't know yet and leave with a design their architects accept, our engineers can build, and core engineering can live with.
Decide whether we build, configure, or refuse. Some asks are a week of configuration, some are a real build, and some would fork the product. You make that call early, in writing, and you defend it to the customer and to our own leadership.
Own the pattern for putting the coach inside a customer's front door. That means agent-to-agent integration on standard protocols like MCP and A2A, into Copilot, Teams, and customers' own agent platforms, designed once so the fifth customer is configuration.
Write the engineering standards for Forward Deployment. The security bar for customer-facing builds, sandbox and data isolation, customer-data handling, and what "ready to graduate" means. Our code touches HR systems and member data at customers who run us through security review, and the standards are yours to write and hold.
Own the seam with core engineering. Every custom build ends one of three ways: it graduates into the platform with core engineering's acceptance, it converts to paid work, or we kill it. You make the technical case at the monthly graduation board, and you design builds so the ones worth keeping can be accepted cleanly.
Build the shared deployment infrastructure. A real customer sandbox, the tooling that turns a customer's own material into a working context library, and the evaluation harness that tells us whether a configured coach behaves the way that customer needs. Each new account should start from what the last one built.
Carry the technical relationship where the decision sits. You'll work with a customer's CTO, CISO, and enterprise architects, and you'll write the answers on data hosting, model training, and legal holds that their governance committee asks for.
Keep building. You write code on the hardest problems yourself, and the first version of every shared pattern is yours.
Raise the bar for every Forward Deployed engineer. You won't manage people. The way you design, review, and document becomes how the other squads work.

What You'll Bring

7+ years building and shipping production software, including several years as the technical owner of systems deployed inside large enterprises.
A record of leading the technical side of customer deployments where the contract value ran into seven or eight figures.
Architecture depth across identity, data, and integration: single sign-on and provisioning, HRIS, data pipelines, and multi-tenant isolation. You've designed for a customer's security review and passed it.
Production experience with LLM and agent systems: tool use, retrieval and context, guardrails, and evaluation. You've been accountable for how an AI system behaved in front of real users.
Credibility with senior technical audiences on both sides of the table. You've briefed a customer's CTO or CISO and your own engineering leadership, and you've delivered bad news to both without losing the room.
A record of turning one-off customer work into platform capability, and of killing the work that didn't deserve it.
Experience with agent protocols (MCP, A2A) or building inside Microsoft Teams, Copilot, or Slack is a plus.
Domain expertise in organizational transformation, human transformation, or talent intelligence is a plus.

Skills & Competencies

Relentless agency. When something isn't working, you own it and fix it instead of naming the team that should have. Humility about what you don't know, and relentlessness about figuring it out anyway.
Architectural judgment under ambiguity. You pick the simplest design that survives the customer's constraints, and you can say what would make you change it.
The discipline to say no. A happy customer asking for one more thing is the hardest no in this job, and so is telling your own leadership that an ask would fork the product. You can do both without damaging the relationship.
Judgment about what generalizes. You can tell a custom build worth paving into the platform from one customer's snowflake, and you'll argue for the distinction in front of core engineering.
Executive technical communication. You can write the architecture note a CISO's team will read, and explain the same decision to a Chief People Officer in two minutes.
AI-native fluency. Building with agents is your default operating method, and you set the practices the rest of the team builds with.
Comfort deciding on incomplete information. You listen, synthesize, decide, and move. When you're wrong you correct fast and say so. You don't stall waiting for consensus.

Preferred Backgrounds

Senior forward deployed engineers and deployment leads from companies that run this model, who have owned the architecture across several accounts.
Staff and principal engineers or architects from enterprise platforms in identity, HR technology, or data, who know how large customers' systems behave once they're deployed.
Founders, CTOs, and founding engineers who sold into large enterprises and carried the security review themselves.
Applied AI leads who have put agent or LLM systems into production at large companies and answered for how they behaved.

Why This Role

Helping people adapt while AI changes how work gets done is one of the most important problems in the world right now. You'll work on it across entire workforces at many of the world's largest employers, a bigger scale than any one company's internal team gets.
You set the architecture for a function our executive team has named as its expansion lever, on the accounts where the technical answer decides the outcome.
Your work sits on the critical path of decisions worth millions of dollars, and you'll know within a quarter whether it moved them.
You'll build for some of the largest companies in the world, in their environment, with their engineers and architects. Nobody stands between you and the customer. If that's not appealing, this isn't the right role.
The custom work has somewhere to go. A monthly graduation board with core engineering decides what becomes a platform capability, and you're the one making the technical case.
The problems are current. Agent-to-agent integration, enterprise AI governance, and evaluating how a coach behaves across tens of thousands of people are open problems, and you'll work on them with customers who need answers this quarter.
Forward Deployment is a young function with unwritten rules. The person in this seat writes the technical ones.

AI at BetterUp

Our team thrives at the intersection of human expertise and AI capability. As an AI-forward company, adaptation and continuous learning are part of our daily work. We're looking for teammates who are excited to evolve alongside technology – people who experiment boldly, share their discoveries openly, and help define best practices for AI-augmented work. These professionals thoughtfully integrate AI into their work to deliver exceptional results while maintaining the human judgment and creativity that drives real innovation.

Benefits

At BetterUp, we are committed to living out our mission every day and that starts with providing benefits that allow our employees to care for themselves, support their families, and give back to their community.

At Sema4.ai, we're building an Enterprise AI Agent platform that reinvents how knowledge work happens—how people and AI agents collaborate to get work done better and faster. You'll be the hands-on leader responsible for building the core of our product: the Agent framework.

Who You Are

GenAI Expert: You understand how to use LLMs (and other cutting-edge models) to do useful work. You know the common challenges around using LLMs in enterprise settings, the most useful context management strategies, prompting strategies, and the nitty-gritty API-level details such as tool use, prompt caching, multi-modality, structured outputs, model-provider-specific differences, etc. You know the difference between top-p and temperature and you’ve maybe seen emerging works (like min-p). Technical Visionary: You can see around corners in the AI space. You understand not just current capabilities but where the field is heading. You make architectural decisions that will scale as models improve. You’ve grown with the field, tracking key changes, and implementing them when they make sense (avoiding the hype and creating clarity through your vision). You’re the kind of person who may have skipped on GraphRAG after a closer look, anticipated the emergence of truly long context models, and paid close attention to Anthropic’s excellent blog on SOTA retrieval techniques.
Hands-On Builder: You write production code daily. You lead by example, contributing to the most challenging technical problems while establishing patterns for others to follow. You act as a force multiplier to the team around you.

Join our impactful journey at ITA International. As Theodore Roosevelt said, “ The credit belongs to the man who is actually in the arena. ” We ’ re here, standing beside our customers , ready to serve and succeed.

updated.title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer, Ads
updated.description:
Opportunity

Offerwall by Unity is a leading mobile advertising and monetization platform that empowers game developers to maximize revenue and engage users through rewarded experiences. For over a decade, we've connected millions of players with offers that provide tangible in-app value, and we're now building the next generation of that product.

Rewarded advertising attracts fraud. Every conversion attempt on Offerwall and the Unity Rewards app is scored in real time by our fraud detection stack: a prediction service, an online feature store, streaming and batch feature pipelines, and a rules engine that decides what gets paid out. When fraud gets through, money leaks from our advertisers and our business.

We're seeking a Machine Learning Engineer to own the ML side of Offerwall fraud prevention. You'll take our real-time anomaly detection and device risk models from development into production, build the labeled fraud dataset and evaluation methodology the team measures itself against, and modernize how we train, serve, and monitor models. You'll work closely with data engineering, backend, and product partners who own the systems your models plug into.

This is a hands-on role with real scope. You'll be one of a small group of engineers responsible for fraud ML end to end, and you'll have a direct line from the models you ship to dollars saved.

What You'll Be Doing

Ship Fraud Models to Production: Take our real-time anomaly detection and device risk models from development to production, so their output drives payout and blocking decisions.
Build the Ground Truth: Create and maintain a golden labeled fraud dataset, and define the evaluation methodology and baseline fraud-efficacy metrics the team uses to judge every model and rule change.
Own Features End to End: Design and evolve the streaming and batch features that feed our Redis online feature store, partnering with data engineering on freshness, correctness, and lineage.
Modernize ML Infrastructure: Plan and drive the evolution of our training and serving stack, including evaluating a move from SageMaker to Kubeflow and KServe, with attention to latency on the real-time scoring path.
Detect New Fraud Patterns: Investigate fraud spikes, analyze user and device behavior, and turn findings into new detection signals, features, and models.
Operate & Document: Monitor model and feature health in production, write runbooks and data lineage docs, and participate in on-call for the fraud detection stack.

What We're Looking For

Production ML Experience: Several years building ML models and taking them all the way to production, including deployment, monitoring, and iteration after launch.
Fraud, Risk, or Anomaly Detection: Hands-on experience with fraud detection, abuse prevention, risk scoring, or anomaly detection, including working with sparse, noisy, or adversarial labels.
Real-time Serving & Feature Engineering: Experience with low-latency model serving and online/offline feature pipelines (for example Redis or another online feature store, Kafka or similar streaming, Airflow).
Evaluation Rigor: Ability to build labeled datasets from imperfect signals and design evaluation methods that hold up when fraud patterns shift.
Core Technologies: Strong Python and SQL. Working knowledge of a cloud ML platform such as AWS SageMaker, Kubeflow, or KServe.
Ownership & Collaboration: You take ambiguous problems to shipped outcomes with limited oversight, write things down, and work well with backend, data, and product partners. You use AI coding tools to move faster.

You might also have

Experience with ad fraud, install/attribution fraud, or fraud in rewarded or incentivized advertising.
Experience with unsupervised or semi-supervised detection methods such as autoencoders, isolation forests, or graph-based approaches to device and user linking.
Experience migrating ML serving between platforms, or building MLOps tooling on Kubernetes.
Background in mobile ad tech, mobile games, or app monetization.

Additional Details

Base Salary Range: We determine the base salary range for this role based on your primary work location:

Zone A: $178,700 - $232,300

Zone B: $159,100 - $206,800

Zone C: $140,700 - $182,900

This range reflects the anticipated base salary for this position. Beyond base salary, this role may be eligible for equity awards and participation in our company incentive plans (such as annual discretionary bonuses or sales commissions). The final offer amount will depend on several factors, including geographic location and the candidate’s relevant experience, professional background, and skill set.

Benefits

At Unity, we want our team members to thrive. We offer a wide range of benefits designed to support well-being and work-life balance.

Please note: Benefits eligibility, specific offerings, and coverage vary based on the country and employment status.

While specific benefits vary, here are some of the ways we strive to take care of our eligible team members globally: Comprehensive health, life, and disability insurance | Commute subsidy | Employee stock ownership | Competitive retirement/pension plans | Generous vacation and personal days | Support for new parents through leave and family-care programs | Office food snacks | Mental Health and Wellbeing programs and support | Employee Resource Groups | Global Employee Assistance Program | Training and development programs | Volunteering and donation matching program

Life at Unity

Unity [NYSE: U] is the world’s leading game engine, powering play for more than 3 billion consumers each month. The top mobile games in the world, the most played PC indie titles, the most innovative console games, and virtually all of the top XR and Web Games are developed, deployed, and grown in Unity. Unity also enables teams across industries like automotive, manufacturing, and healthcare to design, simulate, and collaborate in 3D — closing the gap between ideas and reality.
